Title: Man charged with murdering student in Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN: An unemployed 19-year-old man was charged at the Kuantan magistrate's court today with murdering a female student.
F. Alan Stevekumar was read the charge by a translator before magistrate Tuan Ruzuaini Tuan Lah.
Wearing a black T-shirt and red shorts, Alan said "faham" (understand) after the charge was read.
He was charged with
causing the death
of M. Elisa Jonova, 19, between 4.32am and 4.50am on Oct 6 at Jalan Air Putih 2.

Title: Police track down hit-and-run driver after fatal Jalan Kuching crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have tracked down the driver of a BYD Seal involved in a six-vehicle crash that killed a five-year-old girl and injured two others on Jalan Kuching.
The
accident occurred
at 3.44pm on Saturday along the road heading towards Segambut from the city centre .
The girl, who was seated in the rear passenger seat of a Perodua Bezza driven by her 30-year-old father, died from severe head injuries while being taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL).
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief, Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa, said the accident involved five cars and a motorcycle during slow-moving traffic.
"Initial investigations found that the Perodua Bezza driven by the victim's father was hit from behind by a BYD Seal.
"The collision also involved a motorcycle before the victim's car spun into the right lane and struck three other vehicles — a Nissan Almera, a Toyota Alphard multipurpose vehicle and a Perodua Myvi," he said in a statement.
Zamzuri said the girl's father sustained injuries to his right hand, while the 33-year-old Yamaha 135LC motorcyclist suffered head injuries.
Both were treated at HKL.
He said police had tracked down the BYD Seal driver, who was reported to have left the scene shortly after the crash.
"The 24-year-old driver is receiving treatment at a private hospital in Damansara for a concussion.
"The suspect remains under the supervision of the investigating officer as investigations continue," he said.
Meanwhile, the other three people involved in the crash — the 28-year-old Nissan Almera driver, the 37-year-old Toyota Alphard driver and the 30-year-old Perodua Myvi owner — escaped unhurt.
Zamzuri said the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
He urged members of the public and witnesses with information about the crash to assist investigations by contacting the Tun H S Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station.

Title: A commitment to fiscal discipline and deficit reduction
Article:
LETTER:
The total of RM510 billion allocated for 2027 budget shows the government is really listening to the concerns of the people while also confronting great external challenges in the form of uncertain global economic outlook as well as the on-going Middle East crisis.
The minimum wage raise to RM2,000 from RM1,700 is significant. Even workers pay in the middle of the range distribution has been push upward, where the starting wage benchmark for graduates and semi-skilled workers is set at RM2,500 a month.
The move to exclude the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), those with annual sales below RM50 million, from the increase in minimum wage, proved that the government also take cognizance of the challenges face by  MSMEs in the backdrop of the energy crisis due to the continuing conflict in Iran.
Meanwhile, taxpayers, especially from the middle-income (M40) households, will benefit greatly from the increase in individual tax relief to RM12,000 from RM9,000, what is more with the one-percentage-point reductions in selected resident income-tax rates.
This time, the scope and coverage have been widened, covering postnatal care, care-giving for parents, purchase of sport shoes, tuition fees, artificial intelligence subscriptions, and even selected pet-related expenses.
These will help middle-income earners which currently facing a relentless financial squeeze as their wages lag behind the rising cost of living.
These are crucial measures for the majority of Malaysians to reduce out-of-pocket expenses.
Under the 2027 Budget, the total allocation for subsidies and assistance is about RM80 billion. Again, this is consequential especially from the perspective of cushioning households against the impact of higher oil prices and elevated living costs.
Through the basic monthly quota under the Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95), the retail oil price is stabilised with the 300 litres quota per month was reinstated.
The Budi Diesel, with up to 400 litres a month, is also significant in terms of neutralising the effect of high global crude oil price to the economy and Malaysians at large.
The STR and SARA schemes have been expanded, another crucial tools to ease the burden of the people. STR recipients will receive up to RM150 monthly, or RM1,800 a year. Even those outside the STR programme will not be left out.
Essentially, Malaysians aged 18 and above who are not STR recipients will also receive RM200 in Sara Madani assistance.
Allocation for Jualan Rahmah and Jualan Agro Madani will increase in the budget to RM750 million, another important measures to ease the cost of living pressure especially for essential and necessity goods.
For first-time homebuyers, particularly those who are self-employed, up to RM20 billion in housing financing guarantees were allocated, helping to boost their financial strength moving forward.
Service tax on elderly care to be reduced from eight per cent to six per cent.
In addition to that, elderly care fees of up to RM96,000 a year to be fully exempt from service tax.
Even minimum pension will be raised to RM1,350. Eventually, all these will ease many issues among Malaysians, especially the sandwich generation who lives in the urban areas.
The government could have done more, but fiscal prudence remains its compass along the way.
Indeed, the fiscal deficit target of below three per cent by the year 2028 remains intact and the government, based on this budget, appears to be on the right track.
ASSOC. PROF. DR. IRWAN SHAH ZAINAL ABIDIN
Senior Associate Fellow
Economic and Financial Policy Institute (ECOFI)
Universiti Utara Malaysia
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chin Hin Group launches sales gallery for RM814mil residential project in Segambut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Chin Hin Group Property (CHGP) has launched the sales gallery for Ophira Resort Residences, the company's latest nature-themed residential launch, offering a resort-inspired living experience.
Set across 1.92 hectares of freehold land along Jalan Segambut, the serviced apartment development offers a harmonious sanctuary where nature meets the modern sophistication of Kuala Lumpur.
Chang Tze Yoong, executive director and group chief executive officer of CHGP, said, Ophira Resort Residences reflects the company's vision of creating homes that go beyond the conventional boundaries of urban living.
He said every detail, from the resort-inspired architecture and adaptable layouts to the carefully curated amenities and premium finishes, has been thoughtfully planned to support the evolving needs of modern homeowners.
"We wanted to design a true sanctuary where residents can enjoy the seamless convenience and connectivity of city life while being enveloped in a sense of tranquillity and nature," Chang said in a statement.
The two-block development features units ranging from 525 to 1,020 sq. ft., with configurations ranging from one-plus-one to four bedrooms to cater to a variety of household sizes and lifestyle needs.
The development has an estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM814 million, with prices starting from RM438,000.
Construction is targeted for completion by the fourth quarter of 2031.

Title: Marine police seize contraband cigarettes, liquor worth RM727k in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Marine police arrested two foreign men and seized 180,000 cigarettes and 7,860.64 litres of liquor worth RM727,351.71, including taxes, in Kubang Semang.
The seizure followed a raid on an unnumbered premises in Kubang Semang last Friday. The operation was conducted by the Marine Intelligence Unit of Marine Police Region One, Penang.
The raid was part of a special operation by Marine Police Region One, which ran from Oct 6 to 11.
Marine Police Region One commander, Assistant Commissioner Jaffri Bidin, said the raid followed intelligence on the alleged smuggling of liquor and untaxed cigarettes.
"The raid resulted in the arrest of two foreign men and the seizure of 7,860.64 litres of liquor and 180,000 sticks of various brands of white cigarettes.
"The total value of the seizure, including taxes, amounted to RM727,351.71," he said in a statement.
Jaffri said the two suspects, aged 28 and 36, had been remanded for 10 days from Oct 10 to 19 to assist investigations under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967.
He said the force had recorded 2,042 cases involving arrests and seizures valued at RM174,636,299.60 in 2026, covering various offences.
Jaffri said marine police remained committed to combating the smuggling of untaxed goods and prohibited items, particularly through maritime routes.
He added that intelligence gathering would be strengthened through cooperation with agencies within and outside the police force to ensure the law was upheld.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High car ownership drives Tuhu Car Care's Penang expansion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tuhu Car Care is expanding into Penang with the simultaneous opening of three stores, targeting a northern Malaysian market where car ownership is among the key drivers of demand for automotive maintenance and after-sales services.
"Penang provides a significant market for automotive services," Vincent Chen, the company's regional head, said in a statement.
According to the Statistics Department, 92 per cent of households in Penang owned a car in 2024, close to the national average of 92.3 per cent, highlighting the potential market for services such as tyre replacement, engine oil changes, battery replacement and vehicle maintenance.
Chen said the expansion into Penang marks the company's move beyond Kuala Lumpur into another major Malaysian city as the company seeks to build a multi-city automotive service network and grow its overseas business.
He said the expansion beyond Kuala Lumpur also demonstrates the company's long-term commitment to making automotive services more accessible across the country.
Tuhu Car Care previously established operations in Kuala Lumpur and surrounding areas, where it began trial operations to test its online appointment system, product selection, transparent pricing and in-store services.
The company's model allows consumers to purchase automotive products, including tyres, engine oil and batteries, through its online platform before booking appointments for installation, maintenance and other services at its stores.
Penang's high car ownership comes against a backdrop of sustained demand for vehicles nationwide. Malaysia recorded 870,300 new registrations of four-wheeled vehicles in 2025, including 759,100 passenger vehicles, according to figures from the Road Transport Department and the Malaysian Automotive Association.
Chen said the growing vehicle population provides a potential customer base for automotive after-sales services, as motorists require regular maintenance and replacement parts throughout their vehicles' lifespans.
Tuhu Car Care currently operates more than 20 stores in Malaysia. The three simultaneous openings in Penang represent a further step in its efforts to expand beyond the Klang Valley and reach motorists in other urban centres.
Alongside the Penang expansion, Tuhu Car Care and Continental have introduced three tyre products in Malaysia. The products are designed to address local driving conditions, including frequent rainfall and the demands of motorists who cover high daily and long-distance mileage.
Industry research by Malaysian automotive platform Motorist Malaysia indicates that many Malaysian drivers travel 20,000 to 30,000 kilometres annually, placing importance on tyre handling, ride comfort and wet-road braking.
Looking ahead, Tuhu Car Care plans to expand into additional Malaysian cities, with decisions guided by local driving habits and market demand.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kota Tinggi records highest API reading at 170
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Kota Tinggi recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 170 this morning, as all eight air quality monitoring stations in Johor recorded unhealthy levels.
Environment Department readings showed that Pasir Gudang recorded the state's second-highest API reading at 168, followed by Pengerang (164), Larkin (160), Tangkak (156), Batu Pahat and Kluang (152 each), and Segamat (129).
PM2.5 was the dominant pollutant at all eight monitoring stations.
An API reading of between 101 and 200 is classified as unhealthy, while readings between 201 and 300 are categorised as very unhealthy.

Title: Plantation earnings face 7pct hit from RM2,000 minimum wage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian plantation companies' earnings could fall by up to seven per cent in financial year 2028 (FY28) due to higher wages, partly offset by stronger crude palm oil (CPO) prices, CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said.
Analyst Ivy Ng Lee Fang said the increase in the monthly minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM2,000, effective June 2027, would weigh on upstream plantation companies, particularly those with a higher proportion of general estate workers earning the minimum wage.
She estimates that higher labour costs could reduce earnings by 0.2 to four per cent in FY27 and two to seven per cent in FY28 for plantation companies under its coverage.
Ng said the estimated impact on 2027 earnings would generally be smaller because the wage increase would take effect partway through the year, with the extent also depending on companies' financial year-ends.
The estimates assume that more than half of estate workers would be affected by the higher minimum wage, although plantation companies do not disclose the proportion of their workforce earning the minimum rate.
"Harvesters should be less affected, as their earnings are generally above the minimum wage," she said in a note.
Ng said the impact is likely to be more pronounced among upstream planters with Malaysian operations, including Johor Plantations Group Bhd, Ta Ann Holdings Bhd and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd.
Over the longer term, higher labour costs could accelerate mechanisation and automation as plantation companies seek to improve productivity and operational efficiency, she said.
This could benefit planters that are better positioned to adopt labour-saving technologies, as well as suppliers of agricultural machinery and equipment.
"Meanwhile, the expanded sales tax refund facility for qualifying machinery and inputs used in fertiliser and pesticide production could provide some cost relief, depending on eligibility and the extent to which savings are passed on to plantation companies," Ng added.
She said the firm would revise its earnings forecasts after clarifying the 2027 Budget measures and obtaining feedback from plantation companies.
Despite the expected cost pressures, the firm maintained its "Overweight" stance on the plantation sector, citing the potential for El Nino-related production risks to tighten palm oil supply in 2027 and support higher CPO prices.
Ng said tighter supply could help offset the impact of rising wages, while planters with higher productivity, greater mechanisation and stronger cost efficiency would be better placed to absorb the additional expenses.
CIMB Securities' top picks in the sector remain IOI Corp Bhd, Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, Genting Plantations Bhd and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd.

Title: RM69bil education allocation to bridge infrastructure gap, boost welfare
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The nearly RM69 billion allocation received by the Education Ministry under the 2027 Budget aims to strengthen national education quality by upgrading school infrastructure and enhancing student and teacher welfare.
The allocation includes RM2 billion to repair and maintain all types of schools and nearly RM1.3 billion to upgrade 682 dilapidated schools, which is expected to bridge the educational facility gap, particularly in rural and remote areas.
Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) Department of Social Sciences, Centre for General Studies and Co-Curricular senior lecturer Dr Nazreena Mohammed Yasin said the funding would help ensure students enjoy a safe and conducive learning environment regardless of location.
"We need to understand that the education gap is not just about differences in academic achievement, but also the opportunity to learn in a safe, comfortable environment equipped with suitable facilities.
"For instance, schools facing issues with buildings, water, electricity or internet access encounter different challenges compared to those with better facilities. Therefore, this allocation has the potential to narrow that gap," she told Bernama.
Commenting on the government's move to expand the deployment of teacher assistants to 200 high-density primary schools, she said it was a step in the right direction as teachers can focus their time and energy on educating, lesson planning, guiding pupils and assessing learning progress.
Nazreena also emphasised the importance of strengthening teaching and learning quality, including critical thinking and digital skills, to ensure the increased education budget yields comprehensive benefits for students.
Meanwhile, Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) Faculty of Educational Studies dean Assoc Prof Dr Wan Marzuki Wan Jaafar said the budget increase from RM66.2 billion this year to RM69 billion next year represents a vital investment in human capital development and the nation's future.
"The next step is ensuring that every allocation is efficiently translated into tangible outcomes, particularly regarding school conditions, student wellbeing, teacher support and access to quality education," he said.
When tabling the 2027 Budget themed "Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values" last Friday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the allocation for school repairs and maintenance had doubled from RM1 billion to RM2 billion under Budget 2027.
The Finance Minister said allocations for National Schools (SK) rose to RM900 million, National-Type Chinese Schools (SJKC) to RM100 million and National-Type Tamil Schools (SJKT) to RM50 million, while the hiring of teacher assistants will be expanded to 200 high-density primary schools in phases following effectiveness evaluations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Girl, 5, killed after BYD Seal rear-ends Bezza in six-vehicle KL crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 5-year-old girl died while two others were injured in a six-vehicle crash along Jalan Kuching Saturday afternoon.
The girl, who was in the rear passenger seat of a Perodua Bezza, died from severe head injuries while being taken to Hospital Kuala Lumpur.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the 3.44pm crash involved five cars and a motorcycle.
He said traffic was slow-moving from the city centre towards Segambut when a BYD Seal rear-ended the Bezza, which was driven by the girl's 30-year-old father.
The impact caused the Bezza to collide with a motorcycle, a Nissan Almera, a Toyota Alphard and a Perodua Myvi.
A video of the accident has gone viral.

Title: Central banks face test. Will they be good cops or bond villains?
Article:
LONDON: A standoff between central banks and their cash-strapped governments may well be looming as an intensifying bond market crunch reopens questions about the political independence of the banks well beyond their interest-rate policy.
Central banks currently appear reluctant to rebuild holdings of sovereign debt, yet those holdings played a significant role in the swelling public borrowing over the past decade. Moving forward, that means either an improbable fiscal tightening will need to emerge or political knives will be sharpened.
Numerous elections in the US, France, Italy and Spain over the coming year mean significant spending cuts are unlikely to be on the agenda. If bond markets continue to tighten — as we've seen in recent weeks — political pressure on central banks to steady the ship will rise even further.
Seeing the problem coming like a slow-motion car crash, central banks are trying to nuance their position.
On one hand, a post-pandemic consensus has built around further "normalisation" of their bond-packed balance sheets. This includes a retrospective disdain for using bond accumulation as a monetary policy tool. On the other hand, policymakers want to keep all options open for temporary fixes in the event of market malfunctioning or another left-field shock.
Bank for International Settlements (BIS) boss Pablo Hernandez de Cos this week laid out some principles for using emergency tools if conditions get rough, using the example of the Bank of England's (BoE) limited and brief support for stressed British gilts during the budget blow-up in 2022.
"A key challenge is to bolster market confidence without overstimulating the economy in the longer term," he said of such emergency tools. "Central banks should try to better distinguish programmes for market functioning from those for monetary stimulus."
But the problem with a middle-ground, only-in-emergencies approach is that sometimes debt markets can get squeezed even when there isn't an acute crisis.
Just look at the current global bond selloff. Markets are not necessarily malfunctioning, and despite the clear energy hit from the Iran war, there's no global shock on the scale of Covid-19 or the 2008 banking crash to justify a red alert. Yet markets continue to inflict maximum pain on government debt-service bills.
Should this continue, alongside a relatively hot AI-infused economy and above-target inflation rates, monetary policymakers could find themselves in a very tough spot. If central banks do step in, the lines between "backstops," monetary policy and direct government support could become blurred, and central bankers could once again find themselves criticised for enabling rising government debt loads.
Yet governments across the developed world may expect them to do just that if sovereign bond yields keep increasing. Rising debt-service bills are coming at a time when ageing demographics in most Group of Seven (G7) economies have already been heaping pressure on pension and healthcare systems, while defence spending is set to spiral higher amid increasingly fraught geopolitics.
Pointing to forecasts that global government debt will exceed annual global GDP by 2030, International Monetary Fund head Kristalina Georgieva this week warned rich governments to deliver credible fiscal-consolidation plans urgently and not fall back on central banks to bail them out.
"I would call these 'monetary cowboys', running to the rescue of the fiscal agents, and my message is: please don't."
HOW DID WE GET HERE?
For context, we need to rewind a bit.
Of the multiple reasons cited for the intense government bond market selloff in recent months, a big question revolves around the gaping hole left in debt markets by the gradual withdrawal of G7 central banks from the swelling debt piles they facilitated following 2008. The selloff has pushed long-term US sovereign borrowing costs to their highest in almost a quarter of a century.
Perhaps the best way to understand how artificially cheap borrowing distorted the picture is to examine how quickly governments accumulated debt when their central banks were buying bonds and effectively underwriting large chunks of it.
The Washington-based Institute of International Finance recently estimated that even though average government borrowing costs across the G7 are back at mid-2008 levels, annual interest expenses are 85 per cent higher because G7 government debts have almost trebled to more than US$60 trillion in the interim.
Advanced economies collectively are now paying over US$3.3 trillion to service bonds alone, it said, which is more than their estimated spending on either AI, defence or clean energy.
But coinciding with, and aggravating, the recent surge in government debt costs has been the steady pruning of central bank balance sheets over the past four years. The aggregate G7 central bank balance sheet peaked at over US$30 trillion in bonds in early 2022 and has been cut by about a third since then. Along with the sharp rise in central bank policy rates to choke off inflation, that one-third reduction has coincided with a 40 per cent drop in long-term G7 government bond indexes and a four-percentage-point spike in their implied borrowing rate.
Have central banks exited too much or too quickly, and should they pause that withdrawal until they rethink it?
BALANCE SHEET PHILOSOPHY
Opinion on the wisdom of so-called quantitative easing (QE)—massive central-bank bond-buying programmes—has done an almost 180-degree turn since the inflation spikes and debt explosions of the pandemic and its aftermath.
For many, the banking crash of 2008 and 2020's Covid-19 lockdowns justified extraordinary one-off balance sheet reactions from the Federal Reserve and others. But many also now criticise the continuous use of bond buying as an ongoing monetary tool, arguing that it underwrote the massive expansion of government debt over the past 20 years.
Much of the central bank world now feels the experiment may have been misguided at best, both because it tiptoed into quasi-fiscal territory and because of a variety of market distortions and inequality questions that arose from what was essentially direct support for wealthier asset owners.
New Fed Chair and long-time balance-sheet-expansion sceptic Kevin Warsh claims the whole 18-year QE episode "borders on fiscal policy". He has already set up one of his Fed reform task forces to look at ways to reduce the balance sheet holdings further.
On the other side of the pond, the BoE is still actively selling gilts, albeit with recent plans to concentrate sales in short-dated paper. And the European Central Bank is still actively running down its balance sheet, which amounts to more than 40 per cent of the Eurozone GDP, even as the region faces echoes of the 2011-12 euro debt crisis in French bond markets. A change of ECB leadership is also on the horizon, and the leading candidates don't appear to have an appetite for a return to the 2010s and the firefighting activism of former chief Mario Draghi.
TWITCHIER TREASURIES
There is also the question of who is holding government debt.
The reduction of G7 central bank bond holdings has coincided with reduced pension-fund demand for long-dated government debt as defined-benefit schemes dwindle and pension savers retire.
Those gaps left by long-term investors keen on safety and steady coupons have increasingly been filled by more speculative, short-term players such as hedge funds, who are much more sensitive to big price shifts, vulnerable to short-term interest rate changes and prone to herding in volatile conditions.
Hedge fund activity in sovereign bond markets has been the focus of regulators for years. While everyone welcomes the demand and liquidity they provide, there is now growing concern about the flipside of that if this "fast money" base gets twitchy.
Some efforts have been made to reduce excessive leverage in government bond markets, but no matter how that pans out, the scale of hedge fund activity in these markets, and by extension the exposure of the banks and trading houses that provide them with leverage, makes for a more skittish environment.
"These buyers are more inclined to sell bonds in response to higher short-term interest rates — funding leg sensitivity — and charge a higher price for the risk of further upward moves," wrote Carlyle strategist Jason Thomas. "When coupled with the growth in the outstanding volume of debt, this new class of investors has left bond markets more fragile and sensitised to front-end repricing."
This sensitivity helps to explain the recent disturbance in Treasury markets, which seems to have been driven largely by the Fed changing course on short-term rates.
SMBC Nikko's rates strategist Joseph Abate cites Fed studies trying to quantify that sensitivity. Fed economist Phillip Monin estimates that hedge fund demand for cash-futures arbitrage plays has increased fourfold since 2020 and is now 3.5 per cent of outstanding Treasury supply.
Another Fed study last month by Daniel Beltran and Canlin Li found that the market's sensitivity to new supply had doubled over the past decade, with every 1.0 per cent increase in new debt, some $300 billion or more, increasing 5-year yields by 8.0 basis points.
Regulators, governments and central banks are watching this closely. But any planned tightening of rules could well have adverse effects at a politically risky moment. While the answer, in theory, may be reducing the supply of government debt, in practice, that is very unlikely to occur.
The alternative solution lands back in the lap of now more hesitant central banks — kicking and screaming perhaps.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KLIA Ekspres services disrupted by cable cut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KLIA Ekspres services were disrupted this morning following a cable cut between Putrajaya and Cyberjaya and Salak Tinggi stations.
In a statement of Facebook, the operator said the combined train service would remain in effect until further notice.
Since 5am, trains have been operating every 20 minutes from both KL Sentral and KLIA Terminal 2, stopping at all stations.
The operator said its technical team was working to rectify the issue and restore normal train services as soon as possible.
Passengers have been advised to check with station personnel for the latest updates and assistance.
The operator apologised for the inconvenience and thanked passengers for their patience and understanding.
NST has contacted the authorities for comment on the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-Bukit Besi assemblyman Roslee Daud dies at 66
Article:
DUNGUN: Former Bukit Besi assemblyman Roslee Daud died early this morning. He was 66.
Roslee, who suffered from heart complications, died at Dungun Hospital at 5.30am.
He served as Umno and Barisan Nasional's Bukit Besi assemblyman for two terms from May 2013 to August 2023.
Roslee also served as a Terengganu executive council member in charge of rural development, entrepreneurs, cooperatives and consumers.
Funeral prayers will be held at Masjid Bukit Besi after Zohor prayers, followed by burial at the Bukit Besi Islamic Cemetery.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Merz Aesthetics steps up expansion amid aesthetics boom
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Merz Aesthetics is strengthening its focus on Malaysia and the wider Asia-Pacific medical aesthetics market as the industry shifts towards skin longevity, personalised treatments and research-driven innovation.
The global medical aesthetics company has launched a regional campaign featuring Hollywood actress Lucy Liu as its ambassador while planning a research and development innovation centre in Singapore to advance research into skin ageing and longevity.
The initiatives reflect the industry's drive to move beyond conventional anti-ageing treatments toward more comprehensive, science-backed approaches that support long-term skin health and natural-looking results.
Asia-Pacific is emerging as a key growth market for medical aesthetics, supported by rising consumer acceptance of non-surgical procedures, growing awareness of aesthetic treatments and demand for more personalised care.
Industry research by MarketsandMarkets projects the regional medical aesthetics market to grow from US$3.75 billion in 2025 to US$8.66 billion by 2031, driven partly by demand for injectables and minimally invasive treatments.
In Malaysia, the aesthetic medicine market has also expanded alongside greater consumer interest in self-care and appearance-related treatments. Market estimates cited in a 2026 industry study put the sector's revenue at RM818.3 million in 2024, up from RM550.1 million in 2022.
As competition intensifies, providers and manufacturers are increasingly focusing on clinical evidence, practitioner expertise and treatment outcomes, while consumers place greater emphasis on safety, credibility and natural-looking results. These trends are also raising the importance of medical training and appropriate clinical oversight as the industry expands.
Unveiled in Seoul, South Korea, the campaign positions skin longevity and personalised aesthetic treatments as key growth areas, responding to changing consumer expectations among women across the Asia-Pacific.
Merz Aesthetics chief scientific officer Samantha Kerr said advances in the understanding of skin longevity were reshaping the medical aesthetics industry, with scientific research playing an increasingly important role in treatment development.
Alongside the campaign launch, Merz Aesthetics announced plans to establish a new Research & Development Innovation Center in Singapore, strengthening its commitment to skin science and its global research and development network.
The planned centre is expected to advance the company's research into skin ageing and longevity. However, details on the investment value, development timeline and operational scope have not been disclosed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK finance minister to call for big economies to get borrowing under control at IMF
Article:
BANGKOK: British finance minister John Healey will stress the importance of budget discipline and improving resilience to geopolitical shocks when he meets his foreign counterparts on his first trip to the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings this week.
"I will work with our international partners  to keep trade moving, support families and businesses, and make Britain's economy stronger and more resilient," Healey said in a statement released by his office.
Healey will argue that major economies need credible plans to get borrowing under control, the finance ministry said, following similar calls last week from IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey.
* The IMF and World Bank hold their annual meetings this week in Bangkok, where finance ministers and central bank chiefs will discuss the impact of the widening war in the Middle East and its effect on energy prices and inflation.
* Healey will meet Ukrainian Finance Minister Sergii Marchenko, among others, to discuss resilience.
* Last week major economies' government borrowing costs hit their highest in decades, driven by investor worries about inflation caused by the US-Iran war, high levels of government borrowing and the need for higher interest rates.
* Healey repeated that he would deliver "fiscal discipline" at his first annual budget on October 28, when he will need to take steps to keep plans to lower borrowing on track in the face of higher debt interest costs and a desire to spend more on defence and reduce energy costs.
* Britain's Institute for Fiscal Studies estimates Healey will need £36 billion of tax rises – equivalent to raising the main rate of income tax by 3.0 percentage points – if he wants to fully offset the erosion of government budgets caused by higher inflation and fund extra defence spending
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Special Branch cop lodges fresh report over alleged assault by Shuhaily
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Special Branch policeman who claims he was assaulted by Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has lodged another police report to provide new evidence.
Lawyers Kamal Hisham Ja'afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin said their client, Lance Corporal Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, lodged the report at the Sungai Besi police station on Oct 10.
In the report, Faiz claimed he was taking photographs on his mobile phone of an incident at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 when his device was seized.
He claimed he was then wrongfully detained, assaulted, manhandled and intimidated.
In a statement today, the lawyers said the facts of the case pointed to possible offences under Sections 186, 323, 353, 355 and 506 of the Penal Code.
The provisions cover obstructing a public servant in the discharge of official duties, voluntarily causing hurt, using criminal force to deter a public servant from performing his duties, assault or criminal force with intent to dishonour a person, and criminal intimidation.
The law firm alleged that Faiz and another lance corporal, Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman, who serve as Travel Control Officers (TCO), were assaulted by Shuhaily in a public area.
The lawyers claimed the incident caused injuries and affected their clients' dignity.
The firm also said it was considering legal action against those who made false statements about the lawyers and their clients, including claims that their legal fees were being paid by a criminal syndicate.
Previously, Ekmal and Faiz denied claims that they
were acting as tout
s or involved in "counter setting".
Today, the firm said the false claims could constitute offences under Section 505 of the Penal Code for statements conducing to public mischief and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act for improper use of network facilities or services.
Last week, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the A-GC had returned
the investigation papers
to the police for further investigation.
Police have recorded statements from 25 witnesses, but several aspects, including verification of CCTV footage, require further examination before the probe can be completed.

Title: Netanyahu demands probe into Gaza film's anonymous Israeli military sources
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Sunday for an investigation into the anonymous sources featured in the award-winning Gaza war documentary "NAZA."
The film is based on testimony from 24 unnamed Israeli military whistleblowers who accuse the army of killing numerous civilians in Gaza with the use of AI-powered targeting systems.
"Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu this evening asked the chief of staff of the Israeli army, the head of the Shin Bet (domestic intelligence), and the state attorney to open a thorough investigation targeting the participants in the film 'NAZA' and to prosecute them," Netanyahu's office said in a statement.
"NAZA" takes its name from the Israeli military term for civilian casualties expected in airstrikes, an abbreviated form of the Hebrew phrase for "collateral damage."
Awarded a special jury prize at the Venice Film Festival, the film received a historic 25-minute standing ovation, but it has triggered a political storm in Israel.
"This film tells a false, misleading and biased story that defames the State of Israel and the army around the world," Netanyahu said, according to the statement.
He has previously declared his intention to back legislation to strip citizenship from people who "defame" soldiers.
The Israeli army, for its part, has "categorically" rejected the accusations contained in the film, expressing doubts about the reliability of the anonymous contributors.
Launched in retaliation for Hamas's deadly Oct 7, 2023 attacks, Israel's military campaign in Gaza has killed more than 74,000 people, according to the territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTViral: Two lorries destroyed, two factories damaged in Bukit Puchong fire [WATCH]
Article:
PUCHONG: A fire in Bandar Bukit Puchong yesterday destroyed two lorries and damaged two factories.
Videos of the blaze, showing thick black smoke billowing over the premises as flames engulfed part of a factory, have since gone viral on social media.
"The operations commander reported that the fire involved two factories," the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department said in a statement issued at 7.10pm.
The premises belonged to Armlink Machinery Removal Sdn Bhd and Skymatics Holdings Sdn Bhd.
View on Threads
The Armlink Machinery Removal factory, measuring 80 by 100 sq ft, was estimated to be 80 per cent damaged, while the 240 by 200 sq ft Skymatics Holdings factory sustained about 30 per cent damage.
"The fire also involved two lorries, which were 100 per cent burnt," the department said.
A total of 24 firefighters were deployed, along with a compact fire rescue tender, two fire rescue tenders and three water tankers.
The department said volunteer fire brigades from Pandan Indah and Serdang were also on their way to the scene at the time.
One post on Threads, which has garnered more than 25,000 views, showed a firefighter working amid thick smoke beside a box lorry at the scene.
"If a lot of people saw smoke from Seri Kembangan or Puchong, I think this is what I saw in a live earlier. The location is in Bukit Puchong," wrote user @mhdalif_96.
Another video showed flames engulfing a factory behind a blue gate, with a white box lorry parked near the entrance.

Title: Lula stages mass rally ahead of Brazil's presidential run-off
Article:
SAO PAULO: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva led a massive rally Sunday to call for more days off for workers ahead of an election runoff against his right-wing opponent Flavio Bolsonaro.
A sea of people massed along Sao Paulo's Paulista Avenue, which was awash in red, the color of Lula's Workers' Party.
The leftist leader, vying for a fourth term in office, is trying to regain ground on Bolsonaro who was the surprise winner of the first-round vote on October 4.
Polls show the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro is favoured to win the October 25 runoff.
While Bolsonaro has proposed a plan to cut public spending, inspired by Argentina's Javier Milei, Lula is looking to make improved working conditions a key plank of his campaign.
The Senate is due to vote Wednesday on legislation, approved by the lower house in May, to increase weekly paid days off from one to two, and reduce the maximum working week from 44 to 40 hours.
Bolsonaro "has to say whether he is in favor of workers resting more or continuing to work longer hours," Lula told reporters.
Bolsonaro has labeled the proposal as "opportunistic." --AFP

Title: Gold steady as markets strap in for US inflation data
Article:
BENGALURU: Gold prices were flat in early Asian trading on Monday, as market participants braced for key US inflation data this week that could offer fresh clues on the Federal Reserve's next interest rate move.
Spot gold steadied at US$4,200.23 per ounce by 0010 GMT after hitting a one-week high on Friday. US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.20 per cent to US$4,225.50.
Key data due this week include the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report on Wednesday, followed by the Producer Price Index (PPI) and retail sales data on Thursday.
In September, the US central bank raised interest rates by 25 basis points. Traders are currently assigning an 18 per cent probability to a rate hike in October, while pricing in an 84 per cent chance of an increase by December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
While gold is known as a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates reduce its attractiveness relative to yield-bearing assets.
US consumer sentiment slumped further in early October as the rising cost of living caused by the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.
Global economic growth will likely slow to 2.60 per cent in 2026, down from 2.90 per cent last year, as the energy shock from the Middle East crisis puts the global economy to the test, the United Nations agency for trade and development said on Friday.
Gold demand in India was sluggish last week, while trading in top consumer China was subdued during the holiday-shortened trading period.
Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.50 per cent to US$61.08, platinum added 0.40 per cent to US$1,693.51 and palladium climbed 0.70 per cent to US$1,155.84.

Title: Ringgit opens higher vs US dollar on fiscal discipline pledge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Monday, supported by the government's commitment to fiscal discipline following the tabling of 2027 Budget last Friday.
At 8am, the ringgit edged up to 4.0820/0880 against the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0830/0875.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the government's commitment to fiscal discipline was reflected in its target to narrow the fiscal deficit to 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product in 2027, from an estimated 3.6 per cent this year.
He said the pragmatic approach should help preserve Malaysia's sovereign credit rating, providing firm support for the ringgit.
However, he said external conditions remained uncertain, particularly developments in Middle East and their potential impact on global crude oil prices.
"Hence, attention will be on whether the US Federal Reserve will consider raising interest rates further this month.
"Therefore, we expect the ringgit-US dollar pair to maintain its tight-range bias today," he told Bernama.
At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major and Asean currencies.
The local note strengthened against the British pound to 5.4038/4117 from 5.4063/4123 at Friday's close and rose against the euro to 4.5735/5802 from 4.5807/5858 previously. However, it weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5806/5846 from 2.5791/5821 on Friday.
Against Asean currencies, the ringgit edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1876/1928 from 3.1896/1934 at Friday's close and the Thai baht to 12.1720/1957 from 12.1735/1909 previously.
The local note also ticked up against the Indonesian rupiah to 228.0/228.4 from 228.1/228.4 at Friday's close, while remaining unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.50/6.51.

Title: IKEA Malaysia strengthens omnichannel strategy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IKEA Malaysia is evolving its retail approach as changing consumer behaviour and digital shopping reshape how Malaysians shop for home furnishings.
The Swedish home furnishing retailer is strengthening its omnichannel model, combining physical stores, online shopping, home delivery and collection points.
IKEA Malaysia Country Retail Director Takeshi Murai said the upcoming Kuching store would reflect this approach.
The smaller format is designed around inspiration and product experiences as part of a wider shopping journey.
"We want the physical meeting point stores to be a source of inspiration, to be a source of touch and feel," he told Business Times.
BEYOND THE  LARGE-FORMAT STORE
The shift does not mean IKEA is moving away from physical retail, but broadening how customers access its products and services.
Murai said IKEA wanted to get "closer and closer" to consumers, but this did not necessarily mean opening a traditional large-format store in every location.
He said the immediate focus was on making the Kuching store successful while the company explored other ways to improve accessibility.
In Ipoh, consumers can order IKEA products and have them delivered to an IKEA collection point.
The company is also developing services such as online interior design to expand digital channels in its retail ecosystem.
"We are trying not only to bring IKEA stores, which can sometimes take time, but also to bring IKEA closer to customers in other ways," said Murai.
IKEA's retail and product strategy is also being shaped by changes in how Malaysians live.
Murai said the company regularly visits homes and speaks to consumers about their needs and aspirations.
One major challenge identified was storage and organisation, particularly as more Malaysians live in smaller urban homes and apartments.
"So we are trying to support customers by providing solutions that fit into smaller spaces than in the past," he said.
Murai added that  IKEA could draw on its global experience in small-space living, particularly from markets such as Tokyo, to develop solutions for Malaysian consumers.
KUCHING  INTRODUCES NEW RETAIL FORMAT
IKEA Kuching, scheduled to open in December, will be the retailer's first store in East Malaysia.
IKEA Kuching will be smaller than IKEA Malaysia's existing large-format stores, reflecting efforts to develop different store formats for different markets.
Murai said IKEA was continuously exploring new ways of meeting customers, with its stores around the world differing in size and layout.
He said the Kuching format was being developed around the idea that physical stores should complement, rather than compete with, digital shopping.
"The concept brings together the physical store, online shopping, home delivery and collection points to provide customers with greater flexibility."
The new store is also expected to deepen IKEA's presence in East Malaysia while creating local employment opportunities.
[[nid:1553439]]
The majority of employees are being recruited  in Sarawak, while some employees from Peninsular Malaysia have been brought in to provide operational experience and training.
"Our ambition is to develop the Kuching store together with Sarawak and the people of Kuching. That is why about 90 per cent of our recruitment is coming from local people in Sarawak," Murai said.
AFFORDABILITY REMAINS KEY
Affordability is still  a major priority as consumers navigate changing household budgets.
Murai said IKEA had recently lowered the prices of multiple products.
More than 1,200 products are now priced below RM10, while more than 300  are priced below RM5.
He added that  the retailer's integrated supply chain, from product design to logistics, helped it manage costs.
"When we design our new range, we introduce more than 1,000 new products. At the same time, we design the price together with the product."
Murai said global purchasing volumes also allowed IKEA to secure lower costs, supporting its low-price proposition.
He said  affordability was not about sacrificing quality, design or sustainability, but delivering value for money.
"One of the advantages we have is that, by setting the volumes across all the countries and  the world, we can secure lower costs. That is how we achieve low prices for customers.
"It's not only about the price. It's also about quality, design and sustainability."
POSITIVE ON IKEA MALAYSIA'S GROWTH
Looking ahead, Murai said he remained positive about IKEA's prospects in Malaysia as the retailer continued to make its products more affordable, accessible and sustainable.
While he stopped short of giving a specific forecast for the wider retail market, he said IKEA had continued to find better solutions during challenging periods.
"I have been through different times at IKEA, and every time things become more challenging, we find better solutions.
"I am looking forward to how we can develop our retail business to be closer to more people, to be more affordable for more people and to be more sustainable.
"I am very positive about it."
For Murai, IKEA's longer-term measure of success goes beyond store numbers or sales.
"Our goal is to create a better life for many Malaysians.
"If we can deliver one piece of IKEA product to every home in Malaysia, maybe I would call it a success," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil climbs as Mideast conflict, tanker attacks persist
Article:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices extended gains on Monday as the Middle East conflict escalated after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, while two tankers were attacked over the weekend, raising concerns about oil supplies from the region.
Brent crude futures rose 76 cents, or 0.73 per cent, to US$105.48 a barrel by 2304 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$92.44 a barrel, up 59 cents, or 0.64 per cent.
The Houthis claimed responsibility for a Saturday strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, while Saudi authorities reported that people were injured in a new attack on the airport on Sunday.
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war with Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.
Trump also unexpectedly announced on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire, following an announcement on Friday of a diesel supply deal with Russia.
In addition, more attacks on tankers sailing through the Strait of Hormuz have been reported so far this month, threatening to dampen a recovery in Middle East crude exports seen in September.
A tanker was struck by a drone near Sohar anchorage, Oman, while another was damaged by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported over the weekend.
Goldman Sachs raised its Brent crude price forecast for December to US$90 a barrel, up from US$85 previously, its analysts led by Daan Struyven said in a note.
"We maintain our base case that continued adaptation of Mideast supply will eventually reduce crude oil prices, while potential renewed escalation still poses significant net upside risk," the analysts said, estimating a risk premium of just over US$20 a barrel.
"We forecast WTI prices, which are unusually low vs Brent because of high US-Europe shipping costs, to average US$81 in Dec 2026 and US$73 in 2027," they added.
In the Gulf of Mexico, energy majors Shell, Chevron and BP were seeking to redeploy personnel and restore production at their platforms after Hurricane Isaias made landfall early on Saturday.

Title: UM MINT, IUCEL put AI-driven teaching, learning in focus
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The UM Mastery in Innovative Teaching (UM MINT) Colloquium and the International University Carnival on E-Learning (IUCEL) 2026 brought together 216 participants from 26 institutions to exchange ideas and innovative teaching practices.
Hosted by Universiti Malaya (UM) at Wyndham Grand Bangsar here on Thursday and Friday, the two-day programme brought together academic staff, researchers, instructional designers, educational technologists, e-learning practitioners and policymakers.
UM deputy vice-chancellor (Academic and International) Professor Dr Hasniza Zaman Huri said higher education is changing rapidly with the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies.
This made continuous innovation in teaching methods, assessment, student engagement and learning design increasingly important, she said.
"We need to rethink not only what we teach, but how we teach and how students learn."
Hasniza added that AI is a key focus of the event, but the challenge is balancing its use with students' ability to think independently.
"AI is our main agenda nowadays. But how do we balance AI and the cognitive thinking process in our students? I think that is the main issue we are discussing.
"We want to encourage the use of AI to enhance teaching and learning, but at the same time, we do not want our students to surrender their cognitive thinking process. That is the key point we are addressing."
She said educators could not avoid the technology and had to ensure it was used responsibly.
"We cannot run from AI. AI is, of course, embedded, but how do we govern its use responsibly? That is our key point here."
Hasniza said UM has an AI policy for teaching and learning. Students and lecturers could use AI, but they had to declare its use.
Sessions on AI and the future of teaching also explored how educators could move beyond content delivery to develop human capabilities.
The programme also featured human-centred e-learning and cybergogy, which Hasniza said went beyond using technology for its own sake.
Instead, it focused on supporting active, collaborative and personalised learning.
[[nid:1553407]]
She added that technology had to keep the younger generation engaged.
"Our technology should be able to enhance teaching and learning, especially for the new generation. We have to come up with something innovative and creative so that our students will be more attentive in class and more excited to attend lessons," she said.
UM MINT, themed "The Future of Teaching Mastery", focused on teaching excellence, reflective practice and the sharing of innovative approaches.
It included the Spark & Share Rapid Talks Colloquium, where educators presented practical approaches involving digital tools, innovative assessment strategies, evidence-based practices and lessons from classroom implementation.
Meanwhile, IUCEL 2026, themed "Redefining Cybergogy Beyond Algorithms", highlighted transformative e-learning, digital innovation and human-centred approaches to education.
IUCEL is an annual conference, with Universiti Malaya co-hosting the 2026 edition in collaboration with the Majlis Ketua-Ketua e-Pembelajaran IPTA Malaysia and the Higher Education Ministry . A key component was the Invention, Innovation and Design on E-Learning (IIDEL) Competition. Participants showcased original technology-enhanced learning innovations supporting inclusive, accessible, collaborative and sustainable digital education.
Hasniza said five main awards were presented. Two went to UM, while Universiti Malaysia Sabah, Taylor's University and Universiti Malaysia Perlis each received one.
The programme included keynote and plenary sessions, workshops, educational technology exhibitions, professional networking opportunities and the IUCEL Awards Ceremony.
Hasniza said the event strengthened connections among educators and gave them opportunities to explore new ideas and identify areas for collaboration.
It also encouraged them to translate those ideas into meaningful changes at their respective institutions.
Hasniza added that UM used new technologies showcased at the event to support its teaching and learning.
She said UM MINT would continue to provide a platform for academics to share, exchange and learn from innovative teaching and learning practices.
"Our aim is to build a continuing community of educators who reflect on their practice, experiment with new approaches and collectively shape the future of teaching and learning in higher education.
"UM MINT is more than a teaching colloquium. It is a UM platform to encourage educators to reflect, innovate and rethink how we teach in a rapidly changing world."
Hasniza said the event, together with IUCEL, brought teaching innovation and human-centred digital learning into one conversation.

Title: Why strategic communication is becoming a leadership competency
Article:
A company announces a major transformation. The chief executive officer uses sophisticated but polished language and tells employees that the organisation will become more digital, agile and customer-focussed.
The employees applaud. Six months later, little has changed. Perhaps the employees understood the announcement but did not understand what it meant for their work.
The above shows why a strategy can be sound on paper but fail if people don't understand what it means for their work.
It underscores the importance of strategic communication and why it is becoming an important leadership competency needed to bring decisions into fruition.
Communication in an organisation no longer means simply transmitting information; it also means providing context to employees.
While in ordinary communication, it may be enough to say "We are restructuring our organisation, strategic communication needs to explain why we are restructuring, what problem we trying to resolve, what it means for employees and where we are going".
Employees today don't just need information; they need context and meaning.
A leader must connect strategy, purpose and action. It is therefore even more important for the leader to explain why.
In an environment that is in a constant state of flux with AI, digitalisation, restructuring, new markets and changing customer expectations, if employees are to be committed to change, it is important that they are told why the change is necessary.
Telling people what to do creates compliance. Explaining why it matters can create commitment.
Nokia provides an example of what can happen when an organisation recognises the need for change but struggles to translate that recognition into timely organisational action.
By the time Nokia responded decisively to the rapid shift towards smartphones, competitors such as Apple and Google had already established strong positions in the market.
The lesson is that recognising change is not enough. Leaders must communicate the urgency of change clearly and ensure that the message is understood and acted upon throughout the organisation.
Some organisations may not choose to communicate everything hoping to inform employees at the right time.
At a time when information travels at lightning speed, it may not be a good idea to withhold information as it would invariably find its way into the hands of the employees.
When explanations from leaders are not forthcoming, employees simply don't stop thinking but they speculate.
If there is a restructuring on the horizon, all sorts of thoughts would come into the minds such as "Is my job safe, Is the company in trouble, what happens next".
The effect can be demoralising for staff, as when leaders leave an information vacuum, employees may fill it with their own interpretations.
Microsoft provides a useful example.
When Satya Nadella became CEO, he sought to shift the company towards a "growth mindset" and greater collaboration.
The change was not simply about introducing new products; employees had to understand a different way of working and thinking.
By communicating the purpose behind the transformation, leadership could connect the company's strategy with what it expected from employees.
Strategic communication is about two-way communication. It is not only communication that flows downwards but also information that flows upwards from employees to decision makers and leaders.
Frontline employees would know what customers are complaining about, where systems are not working, why employees are resisting change and where the strategy is difficult to implement.
Unless there is a two-way flow of communication, an organisation cannot be agile enough to meet the changing expectations of customers.
It is customary for companies to hire communication professionals, but they still cannot replace messages from leaders.
Communication professionals can help formulate messages, but when there is a strategic change, employees expect communication from leaders.
Communication cannot be outsourced when it comes to key issues within the company because these issues require the voice and presence of the leader.
Leadership was once associated with making decisions, setting targets and giving directions.
In an increasingly complex world, decisions would have to be made by different levels of employees, and leaders must explain clearly the thinking behind the decision and elicit feedback from employees who have their hands on the pulse of the customers and the markets.
The leaders of the future must not only know where the organisation is going but also why it is going there.
* The writer holds an MBA from the University of Strathclyde, United Kingdom, awarded under the British Chevening Scholarship programme. With extensive experience in the financial markets and management education, he also served at a prominent think tank. The views expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Business Times.

Title: 2027 Budget: Make growth pay
Article:
THE 2027 Budget 2027 carries a headline figure of RM510 billion.
For a household deciding whether it can afford the month's groceries, school expenses and loan repayments, the more consequential figure is what remains in its bank account.
That is the distance this budget must bridge: between national economic performance and personal financial security.
The budget offers meaningful relief within constrained public finances. Its central challenge is to turn a modest increase in federal spending into a sustained improvement in household purchasing power.
Reconciling growth, household protection and stronger public finances deserves recognition. Yet allocations express intentions. Their value will be established through implementation.
Beyond the RM510 Billion Headline
The first requirement is clarity about the numbers. The RM510 billion envelope includes federal expenditure alongside investment by government-linked investment companies, public-private arrangements, statutory bodies and MoF Incorporated companies.
Their financing and implications for public finances differ. The rise from RM470 billion to RM510 billion, about 8.5 per cent, compares the broader announced envelopes.
Direct federal expenditure, meanwhile, increases from the revised RM444.1 billion estimate for 2026 to RM459.8 billion in 2027: about
RM15.7 billion, or 3.5 per cent. Development expenditure rises from RM81 billion to RM83 billion.
These are different comparisons. The federal increase is nominal, before changing costs, and does not by itself establish the net fiscal stimulus.
Composition and execution will determine the result. Assistance can support consumption quickly. Education, healthcare and infrastructure can raise productive capacity over many years.
Procurement delays and poorly chosen projects can diminish both effects.
Local supplier networks are equally important. Investment generates wider benefits when Malaysian firms provide components, services and expertise, and workers acquire skills that support higher earnings.
Imported technology can raise productivity substantially; the policy task is to develop the skills and supplier capabilities that allow more of its benefits to remain in Malaysia.
Investment in semiconductors, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing and the energy transition must build domestic capacity alongside attracting capital.
Regional development belongs within the same framework. Stronger Penang-Kedah manufacturing connections and better integration of Sabah and Sarawak's production economies can spread opportunity.
Reliable utilities, logistics and supplier development should connect smaller firms and less-developed regions to expanding markets.
The Household Balance Sheet
The announced minimum-wage increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 from June 2027, subject to exemptions for qualifying MSMEs, and the increase in individual income-tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000 give substance to the household-income agenda.
The reach of these measures requires attention. Workers employed by firms qualifying for the exemption cannot assume that the new wage floor will apply to them.
Smaller employers need practical support to improve productivity and sustain higher pay, with progress assessed through workers' earnings.
Tax relief also needs precise explanation.
An additional RM3,000 deduction reduces taxable income; it does not provide RM3,000 in cash.
The benefit depends on the taxpayer's circumstances. Households without income-tax liability receive no direct gain from that deduction.
Combined STR and SARA allocations rise from RM15 billion to RM16 billion. Timely assistance matters greatly to families with little financial buffer.
Targeting must, however, reflect how people live. Identical household incomes can support very different living standards depending on the number of dependants, disability, medical needs and location.
Eligibility records need regular updating, accessible appeals and sensible arrangements for households whose incomes fluctuate.
For middle-income families, the deeper difficulty is the cumulative cost of housing, food, commuting, childcare, healthcare and debt.
Occasional relief helps, but these recurring obligations require sustained policy attention.
Affordable homes must be connected to employment. Public transport must be dependable enough to reduce reliance on private vehicles.
Healthcare and childcare must be accessible enough to lower unavoidable expenses and enable people to work.
These services are part of household economic security. Their quality determines how much private spending families must undertake. A wage increase goes further when essential services work well.
Fiscal Discipline Must Earn Its Keep
The fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of GDP, against 3.6 per cent in 2026, is achievable, but conditional.
The 2026 estimate has already been revised from 3.5 per cent following pressure on fuel subsidies.
The Finance Ministry's published baseline projects a modest decline in the deficit from about RM78.5 billion to RM77.5 billion. Growth in the economy contributes materially to the improved ratio.
There is underlying adjustment too: the primary deficit, which excludes interest payments, is projected to fall from 1.0 to 0.7 per cent of GDP.
However, the tables explicitly exclude new 2027 Budget measures. The cost and financing of those measures must therefore be reconciled with the baseline before the full fiscal impact can be assessed.
Weaker growth would affect revenue; expensive energy could increase subsidy costs.
Higher petroleum receipts need not match the timing or scale of that expenditure. Debt servicing, projected at approximately RM61 billion, will absorb about one ringgit in six of federal revenue.
This constrains choices even where the case for investment is strong. Published estimates put revenue at RM380.8 billion against operating expenditure of RM376.8 billion, leaving just RM4 billion before development spending. This narrow margin strengthens the case for sustainable revenue reform.
Better compliance and a review of ineffective tax concessions can broaden the base while distributing the burden more fairly.
Household tax relief should be assessed alongside the lasting revenue needed for dependable healthcare, education and infrastructure.
Building on e-Invoicing and existing reforms, the government should explain what additional revenue will finance and how vulnerable households will be protected.
Public confidence depends on seeing taxes translated into services that work. Operating expenditure should nonetheless be judged fairly.
Teachers, nurses, medicines and maintenance are indispensable to development. A hospital building without sufficient staff and equipment cannot deliver the expected public benefit.
The task is to improve value across the budget: complete useful projects, maintain assets, strengthen procurement competition and discontinue weak programmes.
Public-private partnerships can supplement investment, provided future government payments, guarantees and user charges are transparent.
Fiscal discipline earns its keep when it limits the future interest burden and preserves resources for services, investment and emergencies.
Delaying essential projects or payments merely to improve an annual ratio would undermine that purpose.
Over the coming year, progress should be measured through wages after inflation, employment quality, household savings, investment actually undertaken and service delivery.
These outcomes must be examined across states and income groups, with external conditions considered alongside the budget's contribution.
The 2027 Budget has set a constructive direction. Malaysians should be able to recognise its results in better work, dependable services and greater capacity to save.
That is how growth earns public confidence: by making ordinary life more secure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SJPP guarantees RM123.8bil in business financing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd (SJPP) has facilitated RM123.81 billion in financing approvals for Malaysian businesses since 2009, reflecting continued demand for funding support among enterprises.
As at Aug 31 this year, the cumulative approvals under its current government guarantee schemes involved 148,795 accounts and 90,503 borrowers.
For the January-August 2026 period, SJPP approved RM7.46 billion in financing involving 10,240 accounts.
SJPP principal officer Juanita Rusmini Abdul Jalil said the schemes were designed to facilitate access to financing for eligible businesses through participating financial institutions (FIs).
"These figures indicate continued financing demand among Malaysian businesses. SJPP's role is to administer government guarantee allocations and work with participating financial institutions to facilitate access to financing," she said.
The financing can support working capital, capital expenditure and business expansion.
Under the Government Guarantee Scheme Madani 2026 (GGSM4), eligible businesses can access facilities ranging from term loans and revolving credit to hire purchase, trade financing and bank guarantees, subject to scheme conditions and lenders' assessments.
Eligible small and medium enterprises (SMEs) can obtain financing of up to RM20 million per company under GGSM4, while eligible mid-tier companies can access up to RM30 million.
"The inclusion of eligible mid-tier companies recognises that financing requirements can become larger and more complex as businesses scale up," Juanita said.
GGSM4 makes RM30 billion available across economic sectors, with targeted focus areas covering Bumiputera businesses, halal, tourism, high-growth high-value sectors and export-oriented mid-tier companies.
Wholesale and retail trade, restaurants and hotels accounted for 44.8 per cent of cumulative sector-based financing approvals as at Aug 31.
This was followed by manufacturing, including agro-based activities, at 17.1 per cent.
Construction contributed 13.2 per cent, while finance, insurance, real estate and business activities accounted for 12.3 per cent.
Together, the four sectors represented about 87 per cent of approvals by sector.
SJPP is also streamlining guarantee processing through its Self-Approved Arrangement (SAA), which allows participating FIs to process eligible guarantee applications within predetermined limits and parameters.
In August, SJPP approved 1,798 applications, its second-highest monthly number for the year up to that point.
Financing approvals reached RM1.35 billion, the highest monthly amount recorded from January to August.
About 64 per cent of August approvals were processed through SAA, with an average processing time of one working day.
"Speed and efficiency matter when businesses need financing for working capital or investment.
"Our processes aim to shorten the processing journey for eligible applications while maintaining governance and eligibility requirements," Juanita said.
She added that financing approvals were only one measure of impact, with the broader objective being to help eligible businesses sustain operations, invest and grow.
Verified post-financing data and beneficiary case studies could provide a clearer picture of the schemes' outcomes.

Title: Emoluments, pensions drive higher govt operating spending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Higher emoluments, retirement charges and debt servicing are driving government operating expenditure 3.8 per cent higher to RM376.8 billion in 2027.
This is despite the expected fall in subsidies and social assistance in the 2027 Budget, according to Kenanga Research.
Emoluments, the largest component of operating expenditure, are forecast to increase 2.9 per cent to RM111.6 billion next year from RM108.4 billion in 2026.
This will account for 29.6 per cent of the government's total operating spending, Kenanga Research noted.
The firm attributed the increase to annual salary increments and additional healthcare and education staff, including those required for the two-cohort Year One intake.
Retirement charges are expected to climb 4.2 per cent to RM44.6 billion as the number of pensioners and beneficiaries grows.
The government is also moving towards a defined contribution scheme to manage long-term pension liabilities.
Debt service charges are projected to increase 6.5 per cent to RM61 billion, representing 16.2 per cent of operating expenditure. Domestic debt accounts for 98.4 per cent of the total.
Meanwhile, subsidies and social assistance are forecast to fall 2.3 per cent to RM72.7 billion from RM74.5 billion in 2026.
But it will remain the second-largest operating expenditure component, accounting for 19.3 per cent of the total.
Kenanga Research said the decline reflects continued subsidy rationalisation through BUDI95, Budi Diesel and the nationwide Electronic Cooking Oil Subsidy System.
However, spending is expected to remain elevated following upward revisions to the 2026 subsidy requirements amid higher energy prices.
The projected reduction therefore reflects gradual efficiency gains rather than a significant withdrawal of government support.
Kenanga Research said with the Finance Ministry assuming Brent crude oil prices of US$85 per barrel, effective subsidy targeting and tighter controls on leakage will remain crucial to containing fiscal pressures while safeguarding eligible households.
