Title: 2027 Budget: Consumers, property stocks in spotlight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Consumer and property stocks are set to gain from the 2027 Budget as cash handouts and housing incentives increase household spending power and support demand for homes, according to research firms.
However, the budget's benefits are unlikely to be evenly spread as higher labour costs threaten to squeeze margins in plantations, technology, rubber products, electronics manufacturing services, gloves, construction and selected retail segments.
MBSB Research identified consumer staples and value retailers as the clearest beneficiaries.
It named 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd, MR DIY Group (M) Bhd, Leong Hup International Bhd and Nestlé (Malaysia) Bhd among its top picks.
"The strongest beneficiary is consumer staples and value retail because household assistance is large, direct and explicitly usable for essential goods," MBSB Research said.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) also favoured consumer and property stocks, and identified oil and gas (O&G) and labour-intensive sectors as potential losers.
"Overall, we feel that 2027 Budget is 'for Main Street rather than Malaysia's Wall Street' and we expect a muted market reaction," analysts Jeremy Goh and Felicia Ling said.
RHB Research similarly maintained an "Overweight" rating on the consumer and property sectors, citing continued government support for household spending and homeownership.
CONSUMER SPENDING GETS A BOOST
MBSB Research said the RM16 billion allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara), along with additional Sara payments, should direct spending towards food, groceries and low-cost household products.
The RM750 million allocation for Jualan Rahmah and Agro Madani would provide further support.
RHB Research said adjustments to individual income tax bands and reliefs, including raising the individual income tax relief threshold to RM12,000 from RM9,000, should also support disposable income.
However, retailers may need to improve efficiency to offset higher labour costs, as passing the full increase on to consumers could dampen demand.
PROPERTY, CONSTRUCTION GAIN SUPPORT
Property developers should benefit from stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers extended until end-2030 and RM20 billion in housing guarantees.
The exemptions cover homes priced up to RM500,000, with partial relief for eligible homes up to RM750,000.
MBSB Research favoured Mah Sing Group Bhd and Matrix Concepts Holdings Bhd, while HLIB picked Matrix Concepts and SkyWorld Development Bhd.
RHB Research named Eco World Development Group Bhd as its top property pick and highlighted opportunities linked to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone.
This includes the proposed Nexus Sedenak industrial development, with estimated investment potential of RM12 billion.
Construction companies could benefit from RM83 billion in federal development expenditure, up from the revised RM81 billion in 2026, and projects such as the East Coast Rail Link Phase Two, Penang Light Rail Transit Mutiara Line and Trans Borneo Highway.
The RM2.5 billion allocation to reduce non-revenue water losses could also support piping contractors.
MBSB Research favoured Gamuda Bhd, Sunway Construction Group Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd and Malayan Cement Bhd, while RHB Research picked Gamuda, Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd and Sunway Construction.
RHB Research said public infrastructure and private developments, including data centres, should sustain contractors' workloads.
Reintroducing the variation of price clause for higher industrial diesel and bitumen costs could ease cost pressures.
UTILITIES LEAD INVESTMENT THEME
MBSB Research identified Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and the grid-electrification ecosystem as structural beneficiaries.
This is supported by TNB's RM15 billion grid investment programme, renewable energy initiatives and rising electricity demand from data centres and artificial intelligence infrastructure.
The firm kept its "Positive" stance on the sector, underpinned by the structural growth in electricity demand.
This is particularly from data centres and industrial expansion, which should sustain investments in power generation and transmission infrastructure.
"Meanwhile, the continued push towards energy transition, supported by initiatives such as LSS6, battery energy storage system adoption and the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme acceleration package should provide a sustained pipeline of opportunities for renewable energy developers and EPCC contractors," it said.
RHB Research expects contract awards to accelerate over the next year, creating opportunities for mechanical and electrical players with exposure to utility infrastructure.
"Ongoing cross-border initiatives under the Asean Power Grid involving TNB and Petronas could sustain high-value regional capital expenditure pipelines over the medium term," it added.
Both research firms favoured utilities and renewable energy stocks such as TNB, Samaiden Group Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd.
HIGHER LABOUR COSTS BITE
Research said the higher minimum wage could weigh on plantations, technology, rubber products, electronics manufacturing services and glove makers where costs cannot be passed on.
The minimum wage will rise from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from June 2027.
RHB Research estimated that the increase could reduce annual earnings by 2.2 per cent to 10.3 per cent for selected plantation companies in a worst-case scenario, assuming a RM300 monthly increase for foreign workers in Malaysian estates.
For selected technology companies, including outsourced semiconductor assembly and testing players and electronics manufacturing services providers, it estimated an annual earnings impact of one to 13 per cent if costs could not be passed on.
RHB Research also estimated a roughly 12 per cent full-year impact on core earnings for the glove manufacturers it covers, excluding Supermax Corp Bhd, before cost pass-through.
The impact in 2027 should be lower because the wage increase starts in June.
Despite wage pressures, RHB Research maintained an "Overweight" rating on construction.
It said the impact should be manageable given prevailing industry wages and the project pipeline.
It was "Neutral" on automotive, citing the risk of weaker vehicle sales after four consecutive years of records, although incentives for local electric vehicle assembly could benefit domestic suppliers over time.
HLIB warned that higher dividends from Petroliam Nasional Bhd could support government revenue but limit upstream investment, creating a potential headwind for oil and gas service providers.
"We believe Petronas' increased dividend payout could limit funding available for upstream investments, a potential headwind for upstream service providers including Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd, Deleum Bhd, Velesto Enregy Bhd, Perdana Petroleum Bhd and and Keyfield International Bhd," it said.

Title: Don’t leave contract dentists behind after Budget 2027 doctor absorption, urges MDA
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Malaysian Dental Association (MDA) has urged the federal government and the Ministry of Health (MOH) to grant contract dental officers the same absorption opportunities as medical doctors and pharmacists, warning that trained dentists are being forced out of the public sector after their contracts lapsed without extension.
In a statement today, MDA president Dr Chong Zhen Feng said the association welcomed the government’s commitment to reinforcing the public healthcare workforce, particularly the permanent appointment drive announced under Budget 2027.
While tabling the national budget in the Dewan Rakyat on Friday, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that over 9,000 contract doctors will receive permanent posts in public healthcare facilities next year.
Anwar noted that more than 15,000 contract doctors have secured permanent employment since 2023, adding that medical graduates completing their housemanship will now transition directly into permanent medical officer positions.
The association also highlighted recent assurances by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad that the ministry is actively expediting permanent appointments for contract pharmacists.
“In this regard, MDA respectfully calls upon the Government and MOH to accord similar consideration to contract dental officers, whose contributions to the nation’s public healthcare system are equally important,” the association said.
Expired contracts and public sector brain drain
The association recalled raising the alarm on April 2 regarding the imminent contract expiry of dental officers from the 2021 cohort.
“Regrettably, these contracts have since expired without extension, and subsequent cohorts have faced similar outcomes,” it said, pointing out that this administrative impasse has triggered an exodus of skilled dental practitioners who have already completed mandatory service and accumulated valuable clinical experience.
The MDA warned that this exit threatens the sustainability and accessibility of public oral healthcare, especially for schoolchildren, rural communities, and lower-income families who rely heavily on government dental clinics.
While acknowledging that operational demands and staffing mechanisms differ across healthcare disciplines, the association stressed that all healthcare professionals deserve equitable treatment, transparent promotional pathways, and formal recognition.
The MDA appealed to Putrajaya to reassess the status of affected contract dental officers, open clear avenues for permanent absorption, and formulate a sustainable human-resource strategy to stem the loss of dental talent to the private sector or abroad.
The association argued that the substantial public investment channeled into training these professionals represents a national asset that must be retained within the public healthcare infrastructure.
“A resilient healthcare system cannot be built by strengthening one profession while overlooking another,” the association said, reiterating that oral healthcare must remain an integral pillar of national health planning.
The MDA expressed its readiness to collaborate constructively with the MOH and central agencies to formulate equitable, long-term staffing solutions.

Title: Johor education department says daily closure notices are routine updates, don’t clash with state haze order
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 12 — The Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) will issue daily notifications on the extension of school closures due to the haze, despite the state government having announced a five-day extension yesterday.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the measure was part of the administrative requirements that JPNJ had to follow and was subject to directives and protocols set by the Ministry of Education (MOE).
“I hope all parties understand that these daily notifications are part of the administrative procedures JPNJ must comply with and do not conflict with the state government’s announcement,” he said in a post on his official Facebook page yesterday.
He stressed that ensuring the safety and well-being of students in the state should be the priority for all parties at this time.
Earlier, many parents took to social media to express concern over the extension of school closures in Johor and seek clarification from the state government and JPNJ.
This follows JPNJ’s announcement today that all schools would be closed on Oct 12, while the state government had earlier announced that the closure would be extended until Oct 16, following the two-day closure on Oct 8 and 9.
In the same statement, JPNJ said Home-based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) would be implemented throughout the closure period to ensure that students’ learning was not disrupted.
The decision to allow students at fully residential schools to return home rests with the respective principals, taking into account current risk assessments and students’ safety and well-being.
Meanwhile, JPNJ said the Year 4 Learning Matrix (MPT4) and other related assessments would be postponed and rescheduled in accordance with directives from the Examination Syndicate and JPNJ.
It also said the Specific School Admission Assessment (PKSK), scheduled for Oct 12, had been postponed, with the new date to be announced by the relevant department.
The revised date for the PKSK for affected candidates would be announced in accordance with JPNJ’s directives, the statement said.
JPNJ also said teachers and officers involved were not required to be present during the assessments and instructed schools and PKSK centres to notify parents, guardians and candidates of the changes. — Bernama

Title: Midnight crash near Glenmarie leaves two dead, five injured
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 12 — Two 20-year-old men were killed and five others injured in a midnight collision involving two vehicles at Kilometre 18.2 heading towards Kuala Lumpur early Monday morning.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency distress call regarding the incident near the Glenmarie Industrial Park at 12.27am.
“A total of 14 personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) and Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene.
“The fire engines arrived at the scene at 12.44am and the operation was successfully brought under control at 1.05am,” he said in a statement on Monday.
The crash involved an unidentifiable Proton Wira Aeroback and a Proton Exora multi-purpose vehicle.
Ashrul Riezal said the Proton Wira was carrying four young men. Two 20-year-old occupants were pronounced dead at the scene, while the remaining two passengers, both aged 19, suffered minor injuries.
“The Proton Exora, meanwhile, was occupied by three individuals, namely a 29-year-old woman, a 27-year-old man and a 28-year-old man.
“All three of them also sustained minor injuries in the incident. All victims were handed over to the Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) for further action,” he said.
The rescue operation mobilized one Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) from the Subang Jaya station, alongside another FRT and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle deployed from the Bukit Jelutong fire station.

Title: Man hurt fleeing George Town EV battery storage blaze, firefighters bring flames under control
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 12 — A man was injured in a fire at an electric vehicle (EV) battery storage facility in Jalan Jelutong here yesterday.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said Eugene Chow Hao Jie, 31, sustained injuries while attempting to escape from the facility.
He said the victim received initial treatment from the department’s Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) team before being taken to Penang Hospital for further treatment.
“We received an emergency call at 3.42pm and immediately dispatched a fire engine from the Jalan Perak Fire and Rescue Station to the scene, where firefighters found a fire involving an EV battery storage facility measuring about 10 square feet.
“The fire was fully extinguished at 4.10pm, after which firefighters conducted inspection and overhaul operations to ensure that no hazards remained at the scene,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Fourteen personnel from the Jalan Perak, Lebuh Pantai and Paya Terubong fire stations were involved in the operation, with assistance from the Mount Erskine and Perak Lane Volunteer Fire Brigades and the police.
The operation ended at 5.57pm, and the case was referred to the fire investigation team for further investigation. — Bernama

Title: King Abdullah II arrives in Malaysia for two‑day state visit marking six decades of ties
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 12 — King Abdullah II of Jordan arrived in Malaysia yesterday for a two-day state visit at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
The special aircraft carrying King Abdullah II and his delegation landed at the Bunga Raya Complex of Kuala Lumpur International Airport at 11.13pm, where he was welcomed by Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
Following the welcoming ceremony, King Abdullah II inspected a guard of honour comprising 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment.
This marks King Abdullah II’s second state visit to Malaysia since May 2008.
Wisma Putra, in an earlier statement said the state visit coincides with the commemoration of more than six decades of diplomatic relations between Malaysia and Jordan, established in 1965.
During the visit, King Abdullah II will be accorded a state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara, followed by an audience with Sultan Ibrahim.
He is also scheduled to attend a state banquet and meet Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Malaysia and Jordan share close and longstanding ties, particularly in education.
As of 2026, 1,636 Malaysian students are pursuing their studies at higher education institutions in Jordan, while more than 1,490 Jordanian students are studying at Malaysian higher education institutions.
Bilateral trade between Malaysia and Jordan reached RM993.4 million in 2025, an increase of 15.2 per cent from 2024.
Trade grew by a further 8.0 per cent to RM740.7 million from January to August 2026, compared with the corresponding period in 2025. — Bernama

Title: Anwar tells youths to lead now, urging students to be society’s conscience against corruption and injustice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said youths must embrace their role as leaders of the present, rather than wait for the future, urging university students to serve as the moral compass of society.
He said young people must lead public discourse and boldly champion causes against corruption, exploitation and systemic injustice.
“Why do you talk about future leaders? What makes you think that the young are not leaders in their own right now?” he said in his speech at the 3rd International Young Future Leaders Summit 2026 (iFUTURE 2026) at the World Trade Centre (WTC), here yesterday.
Reflecting on his days as a student activist, Anwar said he had always been cynical about older generations referring to youths as leaders of tomorrow, stressing that young people were leaders of both the present and the future.
“You must represent the conscience of the present. The present society cannot condone corruption, exploitation… and accept injustice. That is the conscience of the present, and the youth must champion this cause with all the strength,” he said.
Anwar said true leadership required moral grounding and empathy, rather than academic qualifications alone, cautioning against intellectual arrogance.
“You may have your PhDs and professorial positions, but you are quite sick because you don’t use your knowledge as dictated by the conscience in your heart,” he said.
To ensure student leaders have the space to exercise critical thinking and voice their ideas, Anwar reiterated the government’s commitment to removing restrictive provisions in the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU).
“No one will be prosecuted just because of their ideas and their criticism, including if the student leader chooses to criticise the Prime Minister. That is not a crime. You have to defend your position, but it’s not a crime to criticise the policies of the government,” he added.
The iFUTURE 2026 summit, themed “Redefining Future Leaders Through Value-Based Leadership”, is the Higher Education Ministry’s flagship initiative, organised by the Higher Education Department in strategic collaboration with Yayasan Perkasa Siswa and Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah.
The three-day summit, running from Oct 11 to 13, brings together 1,231 student leaders, comprising 813 Malaysians and 418 international delegates from 60 countries, to foster international student leadership networks through intellectual discourse and strategic engagement.
Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir and his deputy, Adam Adli Abd Halim. — Bernama

Title: Special Branch cop makes fresh report with new evidence on alleged assault by border control chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — A Special Branch policeman who alleged he was assaulted by Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has lodged a fresh report to submit new evidence.
Lawyers Kamal Hisham Ja’afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin confirmed that their client, 40-year-old Lance Corporal Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, lodged the supplementary report at the Sungai Besi police station on Oct 10,
NST
reported.
In the report, Faiz claimed he was using his mobile phone to photograph an incident at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 when his device was abruptly confiscated. He alleged that he was subsequently wrongfully detained, manhandled, assaulted, and intimidated.
In a statement today, the lawyers argued that details of the incident indicate potential offences under the Penal Code, including obstructing a public servant in the discharge of official duties, voluntarily causing hurt, using criminal force to deter a public servant, assault with intent to dishonour a person, and criminal intimidation.
The law firm alleged that Faiz and a second officer, Lance Corporal Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman, who both serve as Travel Control Officers (TCO), were assaulted by Shuhaily in a public area, sustaining physical injuries and suffering humiliation.
Refusal of syndicate allegations and warning of legal action
The lawyers also announced they are considering legal action against parties disseminating statements targeting their firm and clients, dismissing claims that their legal fees were being financed by a criminal syndicate.
Faiz and Ekmal previously rejected allegations that they operated as touts or were complicit in illicit “counter setting” syndicates at the airport.
The firm warned that fabricating such allegations could constitute criminal offences under Section 505 of the Penal Code for statements conducing to public mischief, as well as Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for improper use of network facilities.
Last week, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar confirmed that his office had returned the investigation papers to the police for supplementary inquiries.
Investigators have recorded statements from 25 witnesses, but several evidentiary components, including the forensic verification of CCTV footage, remain pending before the investigation can be concluded.

Title: Police say Eric See-To released on bail after probe into online post mocking Quranic verse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Social media influencer ‘Lim Sian See’ was summoned to the Brickfields District Police Headquarters (IPD) yesterday to have his statement recorded over an online post.
According to a source, Lim, whose real name is Datuk Eric See-To, was then brought to the Dang Wangi IPD at 12.45am, before the case was referred to Bukit Aman.
The source added that Lim was later released on police bail.
Lim reportedly questioned the use of the word ‘lighad’ in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s speech when tabling the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on Friday.
In the post, Lim questioned the term before sarcastically linking it to another word.
The word ‘lighad’, quoted from verse 18 of Surah al-Hasyr in the Quran, means tomorrow or the future. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Healthcare access gap, Budget 2027 debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Government measures to address the gap in access to doctors, specialists and diagnostic facilities between urban hospitals and rural healthcare facilities will be among the key focuses of today’s Dewan Rakyat session.
According to the Order of Business on the Parliament’s website, the issue will be raised by Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias (BN-Jelebu), who will ask the Health Minister to explain the government’s measures to address the disparity during the question-and-answer session.
Also in focus is a question from Muhammad Fawwaz Mohamad Jan (PN-Permatang Pauh) to the Investment, Trade and Industry Minister on the risks of the country’s export dependence on the electrical and electronics (E&E) sector, which accounts for nearly half of total exports, as well as diversification strategies should the global semiconductor cycle weaken.
Mohd Isam Mohd Isa (BN-Tampin) will ask the Rural and Regional Development Minister to explain the strategic justification for the establishment of the first MARA hospital, including the status of studies and planning, its location, bed capacity, areas of specialisation, estimated development cost, funding sources and expected commencement of operations.
In the same session, Rushdan Rusmi (PN-Padang Besar) will ask the Home Minister to detail the government’s integrated measures to combat people smuggling, drugs and prohibited goods through unofficial routes along the Perlis border, including action against the syndicate networks involved.
Also listed is a question from Jimmy Puah Wee Tse (PH-Tebrau) on the government’s long-term policies to address climate change and the implementation timeline for the postponed carbon tax to ensure Malaysia’s competitiveness in a low-carbon economy.
Kamal Ashaari (PN-Kuala Krau) will ask the Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development Minister to explain the monitoring measures and interventions in place to ensure that Koperasi Permodalan Felda Malaysia Berhad (KPF) settles outstanding share redemption payments owed to more than 9,000 members, including the setting of a payment timeline.
This week’s Dewan Rakyat sitting will also see the start of the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027, following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, on Friday.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, the policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 will run from Oct 12 to 22, followed by a four-day winding-up session by relevant ministers beginning Oct 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting will run for 37 days until Dec 8. — Bernama

Title: Haze rebounds across 22 areas in Malaysia even as schools set to reopen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Air quality deteriorated across several states this morning, with 22 of the country's 68 monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as schools in multiple states prepared to resume physical classes.
According to Department of Environment (DOE) surveillance data as of 8.46am, only three stations recorded good air quality while 42 were in the moderate range.
Johor emerged as the hardest-hit state, accounting for eight unhealthy stations, including the nation's highest reading of 170 in Kota Tinggi. Elevated figures were also logged in Pasir Gudang (168), Pengerang (164), Larkin (160), Tangkak (156), Batu Pahat (152), Kluang (152), and Segamat (129).
In Negeri Sembilan, Seremban recorded 164, Nilai posted 163, and coastal Port Dickson stood at 137.
Pahang logged three unhealthy stations, comprising Balok Baru in Kuantan at 162, Rompin at 157, and Indera Mahkota in Kuantan at 142. In Terengganu, elevated readings were recorded across Kemaman (157), Paka (156), and Kuala Terengganu (154).
In Melaka, Bukit Rambai logged 153, while Alor Gajah hovered just over the line at 101.
Across the Greater Klang Valley, Putrajaya registered 146, peat fire hotspot Johan Setia in Selangor recorded 129, and Cheras in Kuala Lumpur stood at 123.
Rebounding pollution complicates school reopenings
The morning spike in pollution comes as schools in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Putrajaya, alongside parts of Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, were scheduled to resume regular classroom sessions today following decisions made yesterday afternoon based on 2pm moderate readings.
In Melaka, education authorities had greenlit reopenings after recording sub-100 readings yesterday, including Alor Gajah at 91 and Bukit Rambai at 94. However, both areas worsened overnight, with Bukit Rambai climbing back into the unhealthy bracket at 153 this morning.
In Putrajaya, where authorities noted readings had remained consistently below the 150 closure threshold over three days, air quality climbed from 70 yesterday afternoon to 146 this morning, hovering just beneath the closure benchmark.
Conversely, Cheras registered steady improvement, easing from 152 yesterday to 123 today. Schools under the Bangsar/Pudu District Education Office had been ordered closed yesterday due to localized pollution.
In Selangor, schools under the Hulu Langat, Gombak, and Petaling Perdana district education offices were similarly kept shut yesterday.
Health and education authorities have advised parents, high-risk groups, and students exhibiting respiratory symptoms to wear protective face masks and track real-time air quality updates via official channels.

Title: Police intercept Isuzu Dmax after chase in Setiawangsa, seize machete, sickle, drugs and cable‑theft tools
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Two local men arrested following a police chase along Jalan Wangsa 5, Bukit Antarabangsa heading towards the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2) in Hulu Kelang here yesterday, were found to be in possession of sharp weapons, cable-theft equipment, and drugs inside their vehicle.
Ampang Jaya District Police Chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said both suspects were apprehended when their Isuzu Dmax vehicle was intercepted at the junction of Jalan Jelatek and Jalan Taman Setiawangsa near the Caltex station in Setiawangsa.
“An inspection of the suspects’ vehicle led to the discovery of dangerous weapons such as a machete (parang) and a sickle, as well as cable-theft tools like a manhole opener. Also seized were substances suspected to be drugs,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions, and Section 6(1) of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958 for carrying or possessing offensive weapons in public places.
Investigations are also being conducted under Section 29(1) of minor offences Act 1955 for possessing or conveying property suspected of being stolen or fraudulently obtained, and Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 for drug possession.
Yesterday, several videos went viral on social media showing members of the public assisting police in chasing the two suspects, who attempted to flee after colliding with public vehicles. — Bernama

Title: PS the Children backs Budget 2027 digital safeguards, calls for transparent funding
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Child advocacy group Protect & Save The Children Malaysia (PS the Children) has welcomed the child safety measures in Budget 2027, but urged the government to establish dedicated, transparent funding to guarantee their execution.
The group commended the explicit recognition of online child sexual exploitation in the national budget speech, noting that the screen in a child's hands has become a primary staging ground for abuse.
Key budget pledges include upgrading the police D11 division’s Malaysia Internet Crime Against Children (MICAC) system with advanced analytics, expanding the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s school safety campaigns, enforcing the Online Safety Act, and training 6,000 caregivers under a RM100 million matching grant.
To highlight the urgency, the group cited police statistics of 892 child sexual crime cases between January and October 2025 alone, while an inter-agency study estimated that roughly 100,000 Malaysian adolescents aged 12 to 17 experience online sexual exploitation annually, with half suffering in total silence.
Executive director Amnani Abdul Kadir warned that digital enforcement tools represent only one part of the solution.
"But technology alone cannot protect a child who does not know that what is happening to her is abuse," she said, insisting that school prevention, accessible reporting channels, and survivor recovery must receive equal funding priority.
The group also urged Putrajaya to publish dedicated child protection line items in the budget, mandate digital safety curricula in schools, enforce platform accountability, and strengthen mandatory background screening for all individuals working with children.

Title: Your MP resigned: What happens to their Malaysian constituencies?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — What happens to a Malaysian constituency when their Member of Parliament (MP) resigns?
The question has become a point of discussion after four parliamentary constituencies — Pandan, Setiawangsa, Subang and Petaling Jaya — were left without elected representatives (MPs) following the resignations of Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad, Wong Chen and Lee Chean Chung respectively.
To date, the Election Commission (EC) has determined that no by-elections will be held for the four seats, but there may still be questions surrounding what happens next, or why these resignations occurred.
Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad and Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli raise their hands together on stage during the official launch of ‘Bersama’ (Together) in Petaling Jaya May 17, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Why did the four MPs resign?
Rafizi and Nik Nazmi resigned as MPs for Pandan and Setiawangsa respectively on May 18, after leaving PKR to pursue a new political platform, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
The two said they were vacating the seats to avoid being seen as party-hopping and to return the mandate they received from voters — voting for reforms — when they were elected under the Pakatan Harapan and PKR tickets in the 2022 general election.
Wong resigned as Subang MP on August 10 after three terms in Parliament.
He subsequently said his decision was driven by concerns that he could no longer pursue reforms and defend democracy from within the government and PKR.
As for Lee, his resignation came shortly after PKR suspended his membership for three years.
Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung resigned after PKR suspended his membership for three years. — Picture by Shafwan Zaidon
So why didn’t they simply leave PKR and keep their seats?
Under Article 49A of the Federal Constitution, an MP elected as a member of a political party can lose their parliamentary seat if they resign from or cease to be a member of that party.
Malaysia’s anti-party hopping provisions were introduced through the Constitution (Amendment) (No. 3) Act 2022, which came into force on October 5, 2022.
Under Article 49A, an MP can lose their parliamentary seat if they resign from or otherwise cease to be a member of that party.
By resigning as MPs first, they instead vacated their seats voluntarily, allowing the Speaker and the EC to deal with the resulting vacancies under the separate provisions governing casual vacancies.
This was made possible by the repeal of Article 48(6), which had previously barred MPs who resigned from seeking re-election for five years, as part of the 2022 constitutional amendments that introduced the anti-party hopping law.
There are exceptions. For example, an MP does not lose the seat under Article 49A simply because they are expelled from their party.
The provision also covers certain changes involving independent MPs joining political parties.
This became relevant when Rafizi and Nik Nazmi left PKR and announced plans to join Bersama.
The two resigned as MPs before joining Bersama, saying they did not want to be seen as having switched parties with the parliamentary mandates they won through the PKR ticket under the Pakatan Harapan banner in the 2022 general election.
Rafizi said at the time that vacating their seats would “remove anti-hopping implications” because they were returning the mandate to voters.
Wong had also resigned in a similar route on August 10 before announcing his membership of Bersama two days later.
In Lee’s case, he left on different grounds.
So what happens next when an MP resigns?
File photo of ballot boxes arriving for vote counting during the Pulai by-election September 9, 2023. Under Article 54(1) of the Federal Constitution, a casual vacancy in the Dewan Rakyat is generally required to be filled through an election within 60 days. — Picture by Shafwan Zaidon
The parliamentary seat becomes vacant
In the latest case involving Petaling Jaya, Lee submitted his resignation to Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul on October 2.
Deputy Dewan Rakyat Speaker Datuk Seri Ramli Mohd Nor told the House on October 5 that Johari had informed the EC of the vacancy in accordance with Article 54(1) of the Federal Constitution.
Under Article 54(1) of the Federal Constitution, a casual vacancy in the Dewan Rakyat is generally required to be filled through an election within 60 days.
However, the provision makes an exception for a vacancy arising within two years of the date Parliament is due to dissolve. In such a case, the seat is not filled unless the Speaker notifies the Election Commission in writing that the vacancy affects the numerical strength of the party that constitutes a majority of the House.
The current Parliament began after the 2022 general election and its five-year term runs until December 2027, unless dissolved earlier.
A constituency stays intact
In case there are questions pointing to whether a constituency “disappears”, the answer is no.
Its electorate and boundaries are unchanged, while only the parliamentary seat becomes vacant.
Voters remain registered in the constituency and will elect an MP at the next general election, unless a by-election is held earlier.
Who represents the constituency after the MP resigns?
There is no automatic replacement.
Another MP does not take over the constituency simply because they belong to the same political party or have been asked to assist its constituents.
A political party may continue operating a service centre or appoint someone to handle constituency matters, but that person does not become the elected MP.
After resigning in August, Wong Chen had indicated continuing his work in Subang and will remain engaged with his former constituents. — Picture by Yusof Mat Isa
What happens to constituency services?
The resignation of an MP does not stop work or services carried out in a constituency.
Constituents or residents can continue dealing with government departments and agencies, while political parties may continue providing assistance through their service centres.
As an example, Wong explained his role as an MP and what happens after his resignation.
“The work of an MP is to pass laws, fight for policies — the right policies, pass debate for Budget, all the other things is not the job of an MP like throw makan-makan or gotong-royong.
“All those, people do it for political purposes, I still do mine, last Sunday I took the deaf and mute children to a mooncake festival,” Wong said.
After resigning in August, Wong had indicated continuing his work in Subang and will remain engaged with his former constituents.
“I have explained this situation to the people in Subang, they’re understanding and they’re fine with it.
“For example if they have an issue to deal with certain government agencies, I still help them, these are things that I can do without an office,” he added.
Wong’s case highlights the distinction: a former MP can continue helping constituents, but cannot perform the functions of an elected MP.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had earlier assured that Lee’s resignation would not affect allocations or development projects in Petaling Jaya, saying projects involving schools, surau, mosques, temples and roads would continue as planned.
If the seat remains vacant while the Dewan Rakyat is sitting, there is no elected MP from that constituency to participate in proceedings. — Picture by Yusof Mat Isa
What happens in Parliament?
If the seat remains vacant while the Dewan Rakyat is sitting, there is no elected MP from that constituency to participate in proceedings.
Other MPs can raise issues affecting the area, however.
The vacant constituency also has no MP casting a vote in the House.
“The questions in Parliament come from us (MPs), although I do invite people to send in their questions,” Wong said.
As for two-thirds majority, Wong said the resignations did not affect the government’s ability to secure a two-thirds majority, although attendance remains important when such a vote is held.
The Dewan Rakyat has 222 seats and certain constitutional amendments require the support of not less than two-thirds of the total number of members of the House.
“A two-third majority is needed to pass constitution amendments and for that the government still has two-thirds,” he said.
Although only 218 of the Dewan Rakyat’s 222 seats are currently occupied, the two-thirds threshold for constitutional amendments remains 148 votes.
Article 159(3) of the Federal Constitution provides that the relevant threshold is two-thirds of the total number of members of the House, rather than two-thirds of the currently occupied seats.
The government currently has 149 MPs, meaning it remains one vote above the 148-vote threshold based on the current composition of the House.
If no by-election is required, the next opportunity for voters to choose a representative will be the next general election. — Picture by Shafwan Zaidon
So when will voters get a new MP?
If no by-election is required, the next opportunity for voters to choose a representative will be the next general election.

Title: Temporary lane closures, diversions on Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway starting Oct 12 for elevated U-turn works
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 11 — The rightmost lanes along both directions of the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway will be temporarily closed from October 12 to February 28, 2027, to facilitate the next phase of construction works for an elevated U-turn.
IJM Land Berhad in a statement today said the closure would affect the median-side rightmost lanes of the George Town-bound and Bayan Lepas-bound carriageways.
The master developer of THE LIGHT Waterfront Penang said the lane closures and traffic diversions were necessary to provide a safe working area for the construction works.
“The initial phase of construction for the elevated U-turn was successfully completed in early September, and upon completion, the elevated U-turn is expected to complement the Air Itam Bypass, helping to improve road connectivity and traffic flow along the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway.
“Motorists are advised to plan their journeys ahead, follow directional signage, and exercise caution when approaching the affected areas,” according to the statement.
IJM Land said further updates would be provided as construction progressed, adding that it appreciated the public’s patience and understanding throughout the construction period. — Bernama

Title: Sungai Golok river basin project: Scope, design adjustments aim to provide long-term flood protection
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 11 — Adjustments to the scope and design of the Sungai Golok Integrated River Basin (PLSB) project in Kelantan are among the factors affecting its implementation timeline and cost.
The Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA) said the adjustments were made to meet current needs, taking into account climate change, infrastructure requirements, actual site conditions and the needs of local residents.
“Among the adjustments made were those involving land acquisition, changes to the project alignment and drainage system capacity to ensure that the project’s design and scope were suited to current conditions and that the flood mitigation system could function more effectively.
“These adjustments are crucial to ensuring that the infrastructure provides reliable, sustainable and safe long-term flood protection for residents in flood-prone areas,” the statement said today.
Earlier, Deputy Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation Datuk Seri Abdul Rahman Mohamad, accompanied by senior officials from PETRA and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), visited the project site to assess progress and ensure that work was carried out efficiently, systematically and according to schedule.
A Bernama survey of the flood mitigation works under the Sungai Golok Integrated River Basin Development project in Pasir Mas October 11, 2026. — Bernama pic
The statement said PETRA would continue to ensure that the project was implemented in accordance with the principles of prudent and responsible governance, with the safety and well-being of the people remaining a priority.
“Close cooperation between the Federal Government, through PETRA and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), and the state government will continue to be strengthened to ensure that project-related issues are addressed effectively and in a coordinated manner.
“PETRA also welcomes constructive recommendations and feedback from stakeholders to improve the efficiency of project implementation, while ensuring that environmental sustainability and the well-being of the people remain key priorities,” the statement said.
The ministry also reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that public funds were managed prudently, transparently and accountably, with emphasis on the quality of project implementation and benefits to the public.
It said these efforts would be further strengthened to ensure the more effective implementation of water infrastructure and coastal restoration projects, particularly in mitigating the risks of flooding and coastal erosion.
On the project’s implementation status, PETRA said Phase 1 had achieved 73.01 per cent physical progress, while Phases 2 and 3 had recorded 3.16 per cent and 24.18 per cent, respectively.
“Phase 1 is expected to be completed in July 2027, while Phases 2 and 3 are scheduled for completion in October 2028 and April 2029, respectively,” the statement added. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid to lead Malaysian delegation on five-day China working visit
Article:
BEIJING, Oct 11 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will undertake a five-day working visit to China beginning tomorrow to strengthen bilateral ties, particularly in trade, investment, technology, and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad said the visit, from October 12 to 16, would include a series of meetings with Chinese government leaders in Beijing before Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, travels to Tianjin to attend the World Vocational and Technical Education Development Conference (WVTEDC) 2026.
He said the agenda in Beijing would begin with a bilateral meeting with Chinese Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang, followed by a meeting with Public Security Minister Wang Xiaohong and several engagements with trade companies to explore opportunities for economic cooperation.
“The meeting with Ding is scheduled for October 15 at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, with both sides expected to discuss efforts to strengthen existing cooperation and explore new opportunities in investment, technology, and human capital and talent development, including TVET.
“Cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is also expected to feature in the discussions, covering infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy, telecommunications, trade, renewable energy, and science and technology,” he told a press conference here today.
Norman said the discussions were also expected to follow up on several matters arising from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s meeting with Premier Li Qiang during his working visit to China from Sept 22 to 24, further strengthening the Malaysia-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
He said both sides were also expected to exchange views on their shared commitment to maintaining regional peace and stability through the Asean-China framework, as well as addressing global issues of mutual concern.
Norman said that in Tianjin, the Deputy Prime Minister would attend a dinner hosted by Chinese Education Minister Huai Jinpeng before delivering a keynote address at the opening session of WVTEDC 2026 on October 16.
He said Ahmad Zahid, who is also the National TVET Council chairman, was expected to be the highest-ranking representative from a foreign government attending the conference, which would bring together 21 ministers and deputy ministers from other countries, with participation from more than 100 countries.
Norman said Malaysia’s participation would provide opportunities to share best practices, foster cooperation between educational and training institutions, and strengthen industry ties between the two countries.
He said that during his visit to Shanghai last year, Ahmad Zahid had also sought the Chinese government’s cooperation in training Malaysian TVET students, including through institutions such as the Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) and related agencies.
This will be Ahmad Zahid’s third visit to China since assuming the post of Deputy Prime Minister in December 2022. He will be accompanied by senior officials from the Foreign Ministry, Rural and Regional Development Ministry, Higher Education Ministry and the National TVET Council secretariat.
Malaysia-China trade for the January-August 2026 period rose 35.1 per cent to RM456.68 billion compared with the same period last year. — Bernama

Title: MCMC boosts UMS internet coverage with 1,010 new Wi-Fi access points, says Teo Nie Ching
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has added approximately 1,010 Wi-Fi access points at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) to expand internet coverage on the campus.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said that this initiative is part of MCMC’s ongoing efforts to ensure that the people of Sabah, particularly students and higher education institution (IPT) communities, have access to high-quality internet services.
She added that the initiative is implemented through a project involving the addition of Wi-Fi access points in public universities nationwide, with MCMC utilising its own funds to support the implementation.
“In Malaysia, we have 20 public universities, and MCMC is once again using its own funds to add Wi-Fi access points in universities, and UMS is certainly among the universities involved in this project,” she said during a live interview session with SABAHfm at the Ministry of Communications Integrated Complex here today.
Also present were Bernama Chief Executive Officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin and Sabah Broadcasting Department Director Mohd Yusni Mohamed Ali.
Teo said the addition will make internet coverage on the campus more comprehensive, thereby enhancing internet access convenience for the university community.
In the meantime, Teo expressed hope that the implementation of the second phase of the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) will further improve 4G coverage in rural and sparsely populated areas in Sabah.
She stated that although these areas lack commercial value for telecommunications companies, the ministry will utilise the latest technologies, such as satellites, to resolve connectivity issues.
In conjunction with her visit to the complex, Teo also inspected the development and operations of departments and facilities under the Ministry of Communications, including the SABAHfm Contrabass Studio, the Entertainment and Music Studio, and the television set for the programme “Kami Bah Ini”. — Bernama

Title: ‘Lighad’ issue: Quran must not be subject to mockery, says religious affairs minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The sanctity of the Quran must always be upheld as it serves as the ultimate source of divine guidance for Muslims, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said.
He said mocking or insulting the Quran was an irresponsible act that could hurt the religious sensitivities of Muslims.
Responding to the viral issue concerning the word “lighad”, which appears in Verse 18 of Surah al-Hasyr, Zulkifli said the word meant “tomorrow” and had a contextual meaning pertaining to preparations for the Hereafter.
“The term carries a specific meaning in the Quran and should not be distorted or made a subject of mockery by associating it with other words in a manner that demeans the religion.
“Therefore, all parties must understand the true meaning and context of Quranic verses and refrain from mocking the sacred text,” he said in a statement today.
Zulkifli said mutual respect and responsible communication were essential to preserving religious sanctity and maintaining harmony in a multireligious society.
He said any conduct deemed disrespectful towards Islam should be brought to the attention of the relevant authorities for investigation and appropriate action under the law.
A social media influencer questioned Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s use of the word “lighad” when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat and sarcastically associated it with another word.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said yesterday that the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) were seeking to locate the individual to record a statement to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Zelensky says Ukraine ready to halt refinery strikes if Russia stops hitting energy grid
Article:
KYIV, Oct 11 — Ukraine would be ready to stop hitting Russian oil refineries if Russia curbed its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday, after criticism from US counterpart Donald Trump.
Tensions between the two leaders have flared since Friday, when Trump announced a deal that would see Russia release large amounts of diesel onto global energy markets in exchange for sanctions relief.
Zelensky described the deal as a “weak decision”, saying it would encourage Russia to keep attacking Ukraine, but Trump said Saturday that Ukraine’s strikes were to blame for rising fuel prices.
Prices at US gasoline and diesel pumps have surged since late February, when joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran prompted Tehran to block the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway used for oil exports from the Gulf.
“Ukraine will be ready to stop striking Russian oil refineries if Russia stops striking our energy infrastructure. Any de-escalation steps must be reciprocal and backed by real guarantees,” Zelensky said on X.
Russia has launched waves of attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure since invading in February 2022, knocking out power and heating to millions during winter months.
Ukraine’s largest private energy provider, DTEK, announced fresh power outages in the capital Kyiv on Sunday.
The row between Zelensky and Trump comes weeks before closely-fought US elections dominated by voter frustration over the cost of living. — AFP

Title: Two dead, including baby girl, in Gua Musang crash involving three cars and motorcycle
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 11 — Two people, including a baby girl, were killed in an accident involving three cars and a motorcycle on the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai Road, Kampung Paloh 3, here this afternoon.
The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) stated in a release that the 5.10pm accident also resulted in seven other individuals being injured, including two who were reported to be in critical condition.
According to the statement, the accident involved three Perodua Myvi cars and a Modenas motorcycle.
“One Perodua Myvi driver was reported to be critically injured and trapped, but was successfully rescued by members of the public before the arrival of the fire and rescue team,” the statement read.
All victims were subsequently handed over to the Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) medical team for further action, it added.
Following the incident, a team from the Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station (BBP), which arrived at the scene at 6.08pm, carried out cleanup operations for accident debris and oil spills. — Bernama

Title: Wanita PKR lodges police report against Eric See-To over alleged mockery of Quranic verse
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 11 — Wanita PKR has lodged a police report against the owner of the Facebook account Eric See-To, also known as Lim Sian See, over a post allegedly mocking an expression related to a Quranic verse.
Wanita PKR executive committee member Farahida Fauzi said the report was lodged at the Kuantan District Police Headquarters at about noon today to enable the matter to be investigated.
“I urge the authorities to conduct an immediate, transparent and impartial investigation. If a violation of the law is established, firm action must be taken without delay,” she said in a statement today.
Farahida, who is also Wanita PKR Pahang deputy chief, reminded the public not to make fun of religion to attract attention, provoke others or seek popularity.
Yesterday, Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh urged the individual to issue a public apology for allegedly mocking the use of the word “Lighad”, describing the act as belittling a Quranic verse, a matter that should not be taken lightly.
Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan stressed that the sanctity of the Quran as the primary source of Islamic teachings must always be respected and preserved.
He said any act of ridiculing or insulting the sacred words of the Quran was irresponsible and could offend the sensitivities of Muslims. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak longhouse fire leaves 25 people homeless in Ulu Tinjar
Article:
MIRI, Oct 11 — Three units of a longhouse at Rumah Wani in Ulu Tinjar were completely destroyed in a fire this morning, affecting three families comprising 25 people.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said it received an emergency call at 8.20am, prompting firefighters from the Lopeng and Batu Niah fire stations to respond to the incident along Jalan Sungai Lansat.
The team arrived at the scene at 11.05am after travelling 135km to reach the longhouse.
“The fire involved three units of a longhouse built with non-permanent materials, namely units four, five and six, covering an estimated area of 54 by 100 feet.
“All three units were completely destroyed,” Bomba said in a statement.
The three affected families comprised five, 10 and 10 members respectively. No casualties were reported.
The operation was led by PBK I Abdul Rahman Rosliee, with 11 firefighters from both stations deployed to the scene. They were supported by two Fire Rescue Tenders (FRTs) and a four-wheel-drive vehicle.
The fire was brought under control at 11.20am, and the operation ended at 12.14pm after firefighters completed overhaul work to ensure no remaining hotspots could reignite the fire.
Police and Sarawak Energy personnel were also present at the scene. — The Borneo Post

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan to unveil candidates on Oct 18, says Anwar’s aide
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 11 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will announce its candidates for the Melaka state election on October 18, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expected to personally unveil the line-up, said his political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin.
Azman said the venue for the announcement would be announced at a later date.
“The location of the announcement will be announced later,” he told reporters after attending the ‘Jalinan Madani Rider Jelajah Melaka’ programme, which was also attended by Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abd Halim, here today.
On speculation that he would contest the Paya Rumput seat in the election, Azman said he would leave the matter to the party leadership.
He said PKR was targeting seven or eight seats in the election, including Machap Jaya and Rembia.
The Election Commission (EC) has set October 31 for nominations, November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling, following the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly on September 23.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, N. Sembilan, Pahang, Putrajaya and parts of KL, Selangor to reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang and Putrajaya, as well as several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, will resume normal operations tomorrow.
In KUALA LUMPUR, the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said MOE educational institutions under the Sentul and Keramat District Education Offices (PPDs) would reopen tomorrow, following a decline in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the areas for three consecutive days.
“The latest reading was at a moderate level, with an API of 84 recorded at the CA15W Batu Muda station as of 2pm today. As such, the implementation of Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) and the Work From Home (WFH) directive for these areas has been terminated,” JPWPKL said in a statement.
However, JPWPKL said schools under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would remain closed until further notice, as air quality remained at an unhealthy level, with an API reading of 152 recorded at the CA16W Cheras station during the same period.
It said that to ensure continuity of teaching and learning, PdPR and the WFH directive for teachers and Implementing Group Staff (AKP) under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would continue.
In SELANGOR, the Selangor Education Department (JPNS) said all schools under the administration of the Hulu Langat, Gombak and Petaling Perdana PPDs would remain closed based on the latest API readings.
In a statement, JPNS also said all schools in other districts in the state would operate as usual tomorrow.
“Teachers and parents are advised to follow official updates from the authorities on developments in air quality and relevant school operation directives.
“Further information on school operations and reopening will be announced through the official channels of the MOE and JPNS,” the statement said.
In MELAKA, schools will resume normal operations tomorrow, as air quality readings remained at moderate levels below 100, according to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) as of 2pm, with Alor Gajah recording 91, Bukit Rambai 94 and Bandaraya Melaka 96.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the Negeri Sembilan Education Department also said all MOE educational institutions would operate as usual tomorrow based on the latest air quality monitoring.
It also advised students experiencing respiratory symptoms or those in high-risk groups to wear face masks as a precautionary measure.
In PAHANG, the Pahang Education Department also said all schools in the state would operate as usual tomorrow, with the haze situation and API readings being continuously monitored from time to time through the respective PPDs.
In PUTRAJAYA, the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department (JPWPP) said all schools under its administration would operate as usual tomorrow, following API readings remaining below the 150 threshold.
According to JPWPP, analysis of API readings showed a consistent decline over the past three days, with the API standing at 70 as of 2pm today. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Air quality in Kuching, Miri improves to moderate levels, says DOE
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 11 — Air quality in Kuching and Miri has improved but remains in the moderate category, according to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index of Malaysia (APIMS) portal on Sunday.
Kuching’s Air Pollutant Index (API) reading last recorded an unhealthy level at 2am today, at 111, before dropping to 99 at 3am.
The reading subsequently declined from 153 at 3pm yesterday (Oct 10) to 85 at 3pm today, placing Kuching in the moderate category.
In Miri, the API reading last recorded an unhealthy level at noon today, at 104, before falling to 99 at 1pm.
Miri’s API reading had remained in the moderate category from 3pm yesterday until 11am today, when it rose to 101 before reaching 104 at noon.
As of 3pm today, all air quality monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded API readings within the moderate category.
The readings were Limbang (84), ILP Miri (80), Miri (98), Samalaju (96), Bintulu (94), Mukah (79), Kapit (66), Sibu (87), Sarikei (84), Sri Aman (61), Samarahan (74), Kuching (85) and IPD Serian (70). — The Borneo Post

Title: Digital tools, AI can preserve Dusun language for future generations, says Sabah deputy CM
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — Digital technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), has the potential to become a crucial medium in efforts to preserve the Dusun language, ensuring that this community’s heritage continues to be learned, used, and inherited by future generations.
Sabah Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said that modern technology can be leveraged through the development of digital dictionaries, recordings of Dusun speech, podcast production, and the creation of online learning materials.
He noted that these efforts need to be strengthened through the involvement of the younger generation, educational institutions, and local communities so that the Dusun language remains relevant and continues to be used in daily life.
“When a language is used less and less, we are actually at risk of losing a part of our own community’s identity and heritage,” he said.
“The question is, in the next 50 years, will our children and grandchildren still be able to speak their mother tongue and understand the history, customs, and culture that form the foundation of their identity?” he said in a statement today.
Joachim, who is also Sabah’s Minister of Works and Utilities, made these remarks while speaking at the closing ceremony of the Ranau Dusun Language and Culture Festival in Ranau yesterday.
He also encouraged schools, colleges, and universities to establish collaborations with cultural organisations and local communities to collect and document materials related to Dusun history, language, and culture for use in education and research.
He stated that the responsibility of ensuring the survival of the Dusun language does not rest solely on certain parties; rather, it requires the commitment of the entire community, especially parents and the younger generation, to continue practicing the use of their mother tongue.
Consequently, he hopes that efforts to elevate the Dusun language will not stop after the conclusion of the festival, but will instead be continued through education, documentation, research, and the active use of the language in community life. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Socso offers up to RM150 tax relief for Lindung 24 Jam, Lindung Kendiri contributors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Contributors who remain under the Lindung 24 Jam Scheme, as well as those making mandatory contributions to the Lindung Kendiri Scheme, will be eligible for additional tax relief of up to RM150 under Budget 2027.
The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), in a statement today, said the initiative is expected to benefit more than 8.5 million Lindung 24 Jam contributors and 1.7 million Lindung Kendiri contributors.
“The Lindung 24 Jam Scheme recorded 10,424 claims in its first four months of implementation, averaging 85 claims a day and highlighting the need for protection against risks that extend beyond working hours.
“It is hoped that the incentive will encourage more people to obtain coverage under Lindung 24 Jam, including those who had previously opted out but may now rejoin, while also increasing participation in Lindung Kendiri,” it said.
Under Budget 2027, e-hailing and p-hailing workers will also receive a 35 per cent matching contribution from Perkeso, with the rate increasing to 50 per cent if platform companies also contribute towards their social security payments.
A 70 per cent matching contribution incentive will also be extended to more than 200,000 self-employed individuals across 17 non-mandatory sectors to ease their contribution burden and broaden access to social security protection.
“Perkeso welcomes the initiative and will ensure that all operational and system preparations are in place to enable self-employed individuals to contribute to Lindung Kendiri and benefit from the matching contribution incentive,” it said.
Meanwhile, more than 40,000 religious functionaries, including imams, bilals, tok siak, noja and marbut and takmir teachers, will also benefit from Perkeso coverage funded by Lembaga Tabung Haji.
Perkeso will also provide health screening vouchers to commercial heavy vehicle drivers aged 40 and above under the Safe and Healthy Driver (PSS) programme to facilitate the early detection of health issues and reduce driving-related risks. — Bernama
Note: Perkeso is also known as Socso, the English acronym for Social Security Organisation.

Title: Budget 2027: Nadma to use RM260m allocation for disaster relief centres, equipment, says Zahid
Article:
IPOH, Oct 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) will prioritise the RM260 million allocated under Budget 2027 for establishing more Permanent Disaster Relief Centres (PPKBs) and procuring disaster preparedness assets and equipment, said Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The deputy prime minister said the move would enable Nadma to assist frontline agencies in enhancing their operational capabilities, particularly in dealing with disasters such as floods.
“We want to establish two permanent disaster relief centres in each state. Insya-Allah, with the additional allocation next year, we will add more according to requirements,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said this at a press conference after launching the 2026 National Preparedness Month (BKN) at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.
He said the target of establishing two PPKBs in each state would focus on hotspot areas that frequently experience floods and require the evacuation of large numbers of victims.
On July 6, Deputy Digital Minister Datuk Wilson Ugak Kumbong, representing the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, said during a Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat that 15 PPKBs involving nine states were expected to begin operations in stages from this year as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s disaster management system.
Of the total, one PPKB each in Johor and Pahang has been fully completed, nine are under construction, while the remaining four are at the procurement and planning stages.
Ahmad Zahid also said the allocation would also be used to procure disaster preparedness assets and equipment, such as boats and water pumps, for relevant agencies.
He said the rate of assistance for repairing homes affected by disasters had also been increased from RM5,000 to RM10,000 per family to help victims repair their homes and rebuild their lives after a disaster.
“In addition, aid management has also been improved, with Bantuan Wang Ihsan being distributed to victims while they are at Temporary Evacuation Centres, before they return to their respective homes, to expedite assistance to affected families,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Health Ministry steps up efforts to recruit, retain nurses amid overseas migration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is expediting nurse recruitment and strengthening efforts to retain those already in service through improved welfare support and career advancement opportunities to address the migration of nurses abroad.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the measures include salary adjustments under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), as well as incentives and allowances for eligible personnel, including an increase in the Post-Basic Incentive from RM100 to RM200 a month.
“The MOH’s priority is to ensure that public nursing services remain competitive while safeguarding the welfare of nurses,” he told reporters after launching the National Liver Health Initiative Roadmap 2026-2030 at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, here today.
Dzulkefly said other measures included maintaining the 42-hour working week for nurses on shift duty, expanding training and promotion opportunities, and offering greater flexibility in placements through a mutual exchange system.
He said nurses were among those who benefited most from the mutual exchange system, with recruitment also being expedited to fill existing vacancies.
Dzulkefly said the MOH no longer recruited nurses on a contract basis, with all new recruits offered permanent appointments.
Meanwhile, he said the MOH was working with the Ministry of Finance to expedite the absorption of contract pharmacists into permanent positions.
As of July, 3,545 contract pharmacists were still serving with the MOH, while another 115 were on the reserve list or awaiting permanent appointments, he said.
Dzulkefly expressed hope that the appointment process could be expedited to enable these pharmacists to enter the permanent service. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan targets Tampin parliamentary seat comeback in next GE
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is aiming to reclaim the Tampin parliamentary seat at the next general election, with its election machinery urged to strengthen its efforts and engage voters from now.
Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) deputy president Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said all parties must work harder to restore public confidence and demonstrate PH’s capabilities through its administrative performance and service to the community, Kosmo! Online reported today.
Aminuddin, who is also Negeri Sembilan PH chairman, said winning back Tampin should be one of the coalition’s main priorities as it prepares for the general election, which is expected to be held in October or November next year.
“Make sure we win. We want to restore our dignity in Tampin. Everyone must work and show the people what we have accomplished.
“The people can see who is capable of working and who merely talks big but cannot fulfil their responsibilities,” he said in his speech at the DAP Negeri Sembilan convention in Seremban today.
Commenting on PH’s defeat in the previous Negeri Sembilan state election, Aminuddin said the experience should serve as a lesson, particularly in addressing racial sentiments which were alleged to have divided support for the coalition.
He said a campaign against DAP that played on Malay sentiment appeared to have affected voter support, including in Malay-majority constituencies where PH’s Malay candidates also lost.
